3.grammar: An indeclinable particle/pronoun with a fixed form (it does not change for case). Used for rational beings ('who'), functioning either as an interrogative ('who?') or as a conditional/relative ('whoever, the one who').

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'he concealed / kept secret' — to hide something within oneself, especially speech or a thought, so it is not disclosed.
4.grammar: A past-tense (Form IV) verb in the third-person masculine singular: 'he concealed.' The Form IV pattern (a- prefix on the stem) often makes a verb causative or transitive. The final -a ending marks the completed action of a single masculine doer ('he ...ed').
4.root: س-ر-ر (s-r-r) — secrecy, that which is hidden

5.meaning: A noun meaning 'the speech, the saying, the utterance' — words that are spoken; a statement or what is said.
5.grammar: A verbal noun (the act/product of speaking) made definite by al- ('the'). The final -a ending is accusative, the case typically marking the direct object of a verb — the thing being acted upon.

6.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
6.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.
6.root: — (pronoun/particle; no triliteral root)

7.meaning: A verb meaning 'he spoke aloud / made public / declared openly' — to bring something out into the open, especially raising the voice with speech so it is heard.
7.grammar: A plain past-tense (Form I) verb in the third-person masculine singular: 'he spoke openly.' The final -a ending marks the completed action of a single masculine doer ('he ...ed').

8.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
8.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

9.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
9.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

10.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
10.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

11.meaning: An active participle meaning 'one who hides himself / conceals himself away' — a person seeking to remain unseen or out of sight.
11.grammar: An active participle of a Form X verb (the sta- pattern, which here carries a seeking/self-directed sense — 'to hide oneself'). It is indefinite ('a concealer') and defective (weak-ending): its underlying final long vowel collapses into the two-part ending -in (nunation), the indefinite genitive form such weak nouns take.

12.meaning: By night / in the nighttime — the preposition 'in/by' joined to 'the night,' the dark portion of the day; expressing the time during which something occurs.
12.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, by') on the noun 'the night' (with the definite article al-, its l- assimilated into the following letter). The preposition forces the genitive case, shown by the final -i. Here the phrase marks the time when something takes place.

13.meaning: An active participle meaning 'one who goes about / moves freely / travels openly' — a person out in the open, walking or going on his way visibly.
13.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and.' The stem is an active participle (the sāʿil 'doer' pattern) meaning 'one who goes forth openly.' It is indefinite, marked by the final -un (nunation); -un is the indefinite nominative ending, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence.
13.root: س-ر-ب (s-r-b) — going forth, moving along, flowing freely

14.meaning: 'In the daytime / by day' — 'nahār' is the daytime, the bright part of the day from dawn to sunset. With the prefix 'bi-' it means 'in/during the day'. Made definite as 'the day'.
14.grammar: A definite noun preceded by the preposition 'bi-' ('in/during/by'). The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which is required after a preposition. (The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates in sound into the following 'n', hence 'an-nahār'.)

1.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
1.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

2.meaning: A noun meaning 'ones who follow in succession / who come closely one after another' — used of beings (such as angels) that take turns relieving and following one another in attendance.
2.grammar: An active participle of an intensive (Form II) verb, here in the feminine plural (-āt). It denotes those who repeatedly succeed or follow one another. It is indefinite, marked by the final -un (nunation); -un is the indefinite nominative ending, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence.
2.root: ع-ق-ب (ʿ-q-b) — to follow, come after, succeed in turn

3.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
3.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

4.meaning: A noun meaning 'between, in the midst of, the space separating two things.' It denotes the interval or position dividing one side from another, and is regularly used to express 'between X and Y.'
4.grammar: A noun of place that functions adverbially ('between / in the midst of'). The final -i ending is genitive, which typically links the word to a following noun ('… between … OF …') or marks it as governed by a preposition. Here the -i shows it is bound to whatever noun follows it.

5.meaning: 'His two hands' — literally a dual 'two hands' with 'his' attached. Often used idiomatically for what lies 'in front of' or 'before' someone (i.e. between his hands).
5.grammar: The noun 'yad' (hand) in its dual form 'two hands'. The -ay ending is the dual in the genitive/accusative state (as opposed to -ā for the subject case), used after prepositions or in possessive links. The attached 'hi' means 'his' (the -i vowel of 'hi' harmonizing after the -ay). In construct, the dual's final -n drops before the pronoun.

6.meaning: 'And from / and out of / and among.' A connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'from,' which marks origin, source, a starting point, or 'some of' a larger whole.
6.grammar: Two particles: the connector 'wa-' ('and') and the preposition 'min.' 'Min' indicates origin or source ('from'), a starting point, or partition ('some of'). Particles do not change their endings.

7.meaning: A noun meaning 'behind him / his rear, his back-part' — the region or direction that is at the back of someone, paired with his attached possessor.
7.grammar: A noun of place ('behind, rear') with the attached pronoun -hi ('his / him'). The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following possessor or follows a preposition. The pronoun appears as -hi (rather than -hu) precisely because of this preceding -i vowel.
7.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — being behind, succeeding, coming after

8.meaning: A verb-plus-object meaning 'they guard him / they keep watch over him / preserve him' — multiple agents protecting and safeguarding one person.
8.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense (Form I) verb. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject acting now or habitually: 'they guard.' The attached -hu means 'him' (the one guarded). The -ūna ending also signals the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact, not a command or hypothetical.
8.root: ح-ف-ظ (ḥ-f-ẓ) — guarding, preserving, protecting

9.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
9.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

10.meaning: Command / matter / affair — an authoritative order, or more broadly a matter, decree, or business at hand. The exact sense ranges from a direct 'command' to a general 'affair'.
10.grammar: A singular noun. The final -i marks the genitive case: it typically links the word to a following noun ('… of …') — e.g. 'the command of …' — or follows a preposition.
10.root: ا-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command; also 'amr' as a matter/affair

11.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
11.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

12.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
12.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

13.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
13.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

14.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
14.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

15.meaning: A verb meaning 'he changes / alters / transforms' something — to make a thing become other than it was.
15.grammar: A present-tense intensive/causative (Form II) verb in the third-person masculine singular: 'he changes.' The yu- prefix (rather than ya-) is typical of these derived forms. The final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of an ongoing or habitual fact.

16.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
16.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

17.meaning: "With/by a people," combining the preposition "bi-" (with, by means of) and the noun "qawm," meaning a people, folk, nation, or community — typically a body of men or a tribe bound together.
17.grammar: The "bi-" prefix is a preposition meaning "with" or "by means of." The "-in" ending (tanwīn) is the genitive case combined with indefiniteness, giving "a people"; this genitive is exactly what a preposition like "bi-" requires of the noun that follows it.
17.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; relatedly, a group that stands together as a community

18.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
18.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.

19.meaning: A verb (Form II) meaning 'they change/alter' — to transform something from one state to another; Form II carries the active, causative sense of bringing about a change.
19.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb, third-person masculine plural ('they ...'). The -ū plural ending without a final -na marks the subjunctive or jussive mood — the clipped form used after certain particles (e.g. 'until', 'so that') or negations/conditions.

20.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
20.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

21.meaning: 'Against / with themselves' or 'by means of themselves.' Combines the preposition bi- ('with/against/by') with 'anfus' ('selves, souls', the plural of nafs) and a possessive 'their'.
21.grammar: 'Anfus' is the broken plural of 'nafs' (self/soul). The preposition bi- governs the genitive case, shown by the -i vowel before the attached pronoun '-him' ('their'). The whole phrase functions adverbially ('with/against their own selves').
21.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, person; the inner being

22.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
22.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

23.meaning: A verb meaning 'he intended', 'he willed', or 'he meant' — to direct one's purpose toward something, to want or aim at it.
23.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'), in the derived (form IV) pattern arāda. The bare stem with a final -a denotes a completed action by a single male subject, with the sense of actively willing or purposing something.
23.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, want, aim at

24.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
24.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

25.meaning: "With/by a people," combining the preposition "bi-" (with, by means of) and the noun "qawm," meaning a people, folk, nation, or community — typically a body of men or a tribe bound together.
25.grammar: The "bi-" prefix is a preposition meaning "with" or "by means of." The "-in" ending (tanwīn) is the genitive case combined with indefiniteness, giving "a people"; this genitive is exactly what a preposition like "bi-" requires of the noun that follows it.
25.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; relatedly, a group that stands together as a community

26.meaning: 'An evil / harm / wrong (deed).' A noun denoting something bad or harmful — an injury, offense, or wicked act.
26.grammar: سُوۡء ('sū'') is a noun, 'evil / harm.' The -an ending (accusative with nunation) marks two things: the accusative case (typically a direct object of a verb) and indefiniteness ('an evil,' not 'the evil'); the final -n is the 'tanwīn' of an indefinite noun.
26.root: س-و-ء (s-w-ʾ) — to be bad, evil, to harm or grieve

27.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
27.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

28.meaning: A noun meaning 'a turning back, a repelling, a reversal' — the act or possibility of something being averted or sent back; also 'no averting it' when negated.
28.grammar: A verbal noun of place/action (the ma- prefix forms such nouns) meaning 'a turning back / averting.' The final -a ending is accusative; this is the form a noun takes as a direct object, and notably the form used after the absolute negation particle ('there is no … at all').

29.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
29.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

30.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
30.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

31.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
31.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

32.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
32.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

33.meaning: Other than Him / apart from Him / besides Him. A relational word expressing the idea of being below, short of, or to the exclusion of something or someone.

parts.en: other than, apart from, besides, below

33.grammar: A relational noun/quasi-preposition meaning 'apart from / instead of'. It is followed by a possessive pronoun -hi ('Him'), which puts it in the genitive 'of' relationship; the kasra written under the pronoun reflects this genitive linkage.

34.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
34.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

35.meaning: A noun meaning 'a guardian, protector, patron, one who takes charge of another's affairs' — a defender who manages and looks after someone.
35.grammar: The prefix wa- ('and / or'). The stem is an active participle ('one who takes charge') and is a defective (weak-ending) noun: its underlying final long vowel collapses into the two-part ending -in (nunation). This -in is the indefinite genitive form such weak nouns take, the case typically following a preposition or negation.

1.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
1.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

2.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

3.meaning: A verb-plus-object meaning 'he shows you / causes you to see' — to make a group of addressees behold or perceive something.
3.grammar: A present-tense (Form IV, causative) verb: 'he makes (you) see, he shows.' The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject. The attached -kum means 'you all' (the ones shown); its vowel appears as -kumu to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a connecting (hamzat-waṣl) alif.
3.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — seeing, perceiving

4.meaning: A noun meaning 'the lightning' — the bright flash that appears in storm clouds.
4.grammar: A noun made definite by al- ('the'). The final -a ending is accusative, the case typically marking the direct object of a verb — the thing being acted upon.

5.meaning: Fear, dread, apprehension — the inner state of being afraid of harm or of an outcome. As an indefinite noun it can also function adverbially: "out of fear, fearfully."
5.grammar: An indefinite masculine singular noun in the accusative case. The -an ending (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ("a fear") and accusative, a case often used to express the manner or reason of an action ("in/out of fear").
5.root: خ-و-ف (kh-w-f) — to fear, be afraid, dread

6.meaning: Avid desire, coveting, craving — the acquisitive eagerness for something one wants to obtain. Intrinsically the word carries a sense of greedy or grasping want; in many contexts it is rendered as eager hope or longing for some good, but its core nuance is covetous desire rather than neutral, noble hope (which is rajāʾ/amal). As an indefinite noun it can work adverbially: "in eager desire, hopefully."
6.grammar: Conjunction "and" + an indefinite masculine singular noun in the accusative case. The -an (tanwīn) marks it indefinite and accusative, a case often expressing the manner or reason of an action ("in/out of eager desire").
6.root: ط-م-ع (ṭ-m-ʿ) — to covet, crave, eagerly desire, be greedy for

7.meaning: A verb meaning 'he produces / brings into being / raises up / develops' — to originate something and cause it to grow or form gradually.
7.grammar: The prefix wa- ('and'). The stem is a present-tense (Form IV) verb meaning 'he originates / brings up,' with the yu- prefix marking a third-person masculine singular subject. The final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of an ongoing or habitual fact.
7.root: ن-ش-أ (n-sh-ʾ) — arising, coming into being, growing up

8.meaning: A collective noun meaning 'the clouds' — the masses of vapor gathered in the sky.
8.grammar: A collective noun ('clouds' as a body) made definite by al-; the 's' doubles because it is a 'sun letter' that absorbs the 'l' of the article in pronunciation. The final -a ending is accusative, the case typically marking the direct object of a verb.
8.root: س-ح-ب (s-ḥ-b) — drawing along, trailing; clouds (which trail across the sky)

9.meaning: An adjective meaning 'heavy, weighty, laden' (plural) — describing things burdened or weighed down, as clouds laden with water.
9.grammar: A plural adjective ('heavy ones') made definite by al-; the 'th' doubles because it is a 'sun letter' absorbing the 'l' of the article in pronunciation. The final -a ending is accusative — the case an adjective takes to agree with an accusative noun it describes (the thing acted upon).

1.meaning: A verb meaning 'he/it glorifies, declares free of all imperfection, extols the perfection of' — to proclaim that the One praised is utterly above any flaw or unworthy attribute.
1.grammar: The prefix wa- ('and'). The stem is a present-tense intensive (Form II) verb of glorification, with the yu- prefix marking a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it glorifies'). The final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of an ongoing or habitual fact.
1.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — swimming/moving swiftly; figuratively, declaring Allah free of all imperfection

2.meaning: A noun meaning 'the thunder' — the rolling sound that accompanies a storm.
2.grammar: A noun made definite by al-; the 'r' doubles because it is a 'sun letter' absorbing the 'l' of the article in pronunciation. The final -u ending is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence — the doer of the action.

3.meaning: A phrase meaning 'with His praise / praising Him' — accompanied by the acknowledgment of His perfect and praiseworthy attributes.
3.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with / by') is attached to the verbal noun ḥamd ('praise'), which carries the genitive -i ending because it follows a preposition. The attached -hi means 'His'; it appears as -hi (not -hu) because of the preceding -i vowel.
3.root: ح-م-د (ḥ-m-d) — praise, commendation of what is good

4.meaning: A noun meaning 'the angels' — the created beings of light who serve Allah and carry out His commands.
4.grammar: The prefix wa- ('and') joined to a plural noun made definite by al- ('the'). Though plural in meaning, it carries the feminine-singular ending -at-/-ah used for such broken plurals. The final -u ending is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence.
4.root: ل-أ-ك / م-ل-ك (l-ʾ-k / m-l-k) — message-bearing; an angel is a bearer of Allah's command

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

6.meaning: A phrase meaning 'His fear / fear of Him / awe of Him' — reverent dread and awe directed toward the One feared.
6.grammar: A verbal noun ('fearing, awe') with the attached pronoun -hi ('His / of Him'). The -t is the feminine-noun ending in its linking (construct) form, since the word is bound to a following possessor. The -i ending is genitive, typically marking possession or following a preposition; the pronoun appears as -hi (not -hu) because of this preceding -i vowel.
6.root: خ-و-ف (kh-w-f) — fear, dread, awe

7.meaning: And He sends, dispatches, or lets loose — to release a messenger or agent and send it forth toward a destination.
7.grammar: 'And' (wa-) joined to a present-tense verb. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') in this causative (form IV) pattern meaning 'to send forth'; the final -u is the indicative mood, the plain present/future statement-form.

8.meaning: A noun (plural) meaning 'the thunderbolts / lightning-strikes' — sudden, destructive blasts of lightning, or a stunning blow that fells or stuns.
8.grammar: A broken plural ('thunderbolts') made definite by al-; the 'ṣ' doubles because it is a 'sun letter' absorbing the 'l' of the article in pronunciation. The final -a ending is accusative, the case typically marking the direct object of a verb — the thing being acted upon or sent.
8.root: ص-ع-ق (ṣ-ʿ-q) — a stunning blast, thunderclap, being struck senseless

9.meaning: A present/future-tense verb meaning 'he/it strikes, afflicts, or befalls'; it conveys the sense of something reaching a target and hitting its mark, often used of a calamity, harm, or blessing that lands upon someone. The opening fa- adds the nuance 'and then / and so', linking it as a consequence of what precedes.
9.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The yu- prefix marks a derived (Form IV) action 'to cause to hit/befall'. The final -u ending is the indicative mood, the normal 'plain statement' form used when the verb is not governed by a particle that would change it.
9.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — to hit the mark, be correct, fall upon (as rain)

10.meaning: with it / by it — a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by means of' joined to a pronoun referring to a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing.
10.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'with', 'by', or 'by means of'. The attached -hā is an object pronoun meaning 'it' or 'her', referring to something feminine in gender. Together they mean 'with it' or 'by means of it'.

11.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
11.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

12.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
12.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
12.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

13.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
13.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

14.meaning: A present/future-tense verb meaning 'they dispute, argue, or contend with one another'; it carries the sense of pressing an argument back and forth, wrangling and quarreling, often persistently and in opposition to truth.
14.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'). The -jādil- stem is a Form III pattern signaling mutual, reciprocal action — arguing against an opponent. The -ūna ending marks 'they (men/people)' in the indicative mood, the plain-statement form; were a governing particle present, this would shorten to -ū.

15.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
15.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

16.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
16.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

17.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
17.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

18.meaning: Severe, intense, harsh, or mighty — describing something powerful and unsparing in its degree.
18.grammar: An adjective on the intensive pattern faʿīl ('severe, intense'). The final -u is the nominative ending, which generally marks the word as a subject or predicate.
18.root: ش-د-د (sh-d-d) — to be strong, intense, severe

19.meaning: A noun meaning 'might, force, severe power'; it denotes overwhelming strength and the capacity to seize or punish decisively. Some read it as the power of a crushing plan or stratagem against which there is no resisting.
19.grammar: A definite noun (with the article al-, 'the'). The final -i ending is the genitive case, which typically links the noun to a preceding noun ('… OF …') or follows a preposition or oath particle.

1.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
1.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

2.meaning: A noun meaning 'a call, an invocation, a supplication'; the act of calling upon someone, especially calling upon Allah in prayer and entreaty. It can also mean a summons or invitation to a cause.
2.grammar: A feminine singular noun. The final -u ending is the nominative case, the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or the thing being described ('X is …'). The tā' marbūṭa (-t-) is the feminine noun ending.

3.meaning: 'The truth', 'the right', 'what is rightfully due' — that which is real, correct, and justly owed; the opposite of falsehood and wrongdoing.
3.grammar: A definite masculine noun (the al- prefix means 'the'). The -i ending is genitive, the case typically taken after a preposition or when the word links to a preceding noun ('… of the truth / by right').
3.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, rightness, that which is established and due

4.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
4.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

5.meaning: 'They call / invite / summon' — to call upon, invite, or summon (also to pray to or call out to); a present-tense verb with a masculine-plural subject.
5.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb, 3rd-person masculine plural ('they call/invite'). The ya- prefix with the full -ūna ending marks 'they (men) do' and shows the indicative mood — the plain statement form ('they do'), with its final nūn intact (contrast the jussive/subjunctive, where it drops).
5.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invite, pray

6.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
6.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
6.root: — (preposition)

7.meaning: Other than Him / apart from Him / besides Him. A relational word expressing the idea of being below, short of, or to the exclusion of something or someone.

parts.en: other than, apart from, besides, below

7.grammar: A relational noun/quasi-preposition meaning 'apart from / instead of'. It is followed by a possessive pronoun -hi ('Him'), which puts it in the genitive 'of' relationship; the kasra written under the pronoun reflects this genitive linkage.

8.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
8.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

9.meaning: A present/future-tense verb meaning 'they respond, answer, or comply'; it conveys answering a call or request favourably — granting, heeding, or accepting what is asked. The derived form adds the nuance of actively seeking or working to answer.
9.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'). The sta- element marks a Form X pattern, here meaning to answer or respond to a call. The -ūna ending marks 'they (masculine plural)' in the indicative mood, the plain-statement form; it shortens to -ū when a governing particle precedes.

10.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
10.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

11.meaning: 'with something / with a thing' — by means of some thing or matter; 'shay'' is the most general word for 'a thing'.
11.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the noun 'thing'. The '-in' ending marks the noun as indefinite ('a thing, something') and in the genitive case required after a preposition.
11.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — thing; to will, to want

12.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
12.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

13.meaning: A descriptive noun meaning 'one who stretches out or spreads open (the hands)'; it pictures someone reaching out with open, outstretched palms — the gesture of one begging or longing for something. The prefixed ka- means 'like / as'.
13.grammar: An active participle (a noun naming the doer of an action: 'one who stretches'). It carries the genitive -i ending because it follows the particle ka- ('like'), which always puts the following noun into the genitive case; the genitive also links a word to a following noun ('… OF …').
13.root: ب-س-ط (b-s-ṭ) — to spread out, extend, stretch open

14.meaning: A noun meaning 'his two palms / his two hands' (specifically the palms or hollows of the hands). The dual form names a pair, and the attached pronoun marks them as belonging to 'him'.
14.grammar: A dual noun ('two palms') with the attached possessive pronoun -hi ('his'). The -ay- form is how the dual appears in the genitive/accusative (the object or 'of' form); the pronoun ending takes -hi rather than -hu because it follows the -i vowel of that dual ending.
14.root: ك-ف-ف (k-f-f) — palm of the hand, to restrain/hold

15.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
15.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

16.meaning: The water — water as a substance, the liquid essential to life. With the attached definite article it points to water as a known or specific body or quantity of water.
16.grammar: A definite noun (al- = 'the'). The final -i ending is the genitive case: it typically marks the word as the object of a preposition or as the second term of a possessive link ('… OF …').

17.meaning: A present/future-tense verb meaning 'so that it may reach, attain, or arrive at'; it conveys something coming all the way to its destination or goal. The prefixed li- means 'in order to / so that', giving it a purpose sense.
17.grammar: An imperfect verb, third-person masculine singular ('it/he'), here in the subjunctive mood shown by the final -a ending. The li- ('so that') is a particle of purpose that puts the verb into this subjunctive -a form, expressing an intended result ('in order that it reach').
17.root: ب-ل-غ (b-l-gh) — to reach, attain, arrive at

18.meaning: A noun meaning 'his mouth'. The base word for 'mouth' is one of a small set of Arabic nouns whose final vowel lengthens when a pronoun is attached, here giving 'fā-'.
18.grammar: A singular noun with the attached possessive pronoun -hu ('his'). The lengthened -ā- before the pronoun marks the accusative case (the object form, or the thing an action reaches). This noun belongs to the special 'five nouns' that show their case by a long vowel rather than a short one.

19.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
19.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

20.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
20.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

21.meaning: A descriptive noun meaning 'one who reaches it / one that attains it'; it names something or someone in the very state of arriving at a goal. Combined with the prefix and pronoun it gives the sense 'attaining it'.
21.grammar: An active participle ('one reaching / attainer') carrying the genitive -i ending because it follows the preposition bi-, which always puts the following noun into the genitive. The attached -hi ('it/its') is an object-pronoun; the bi- here often adds emphasis (frequently in negated statements, '… is by no means reaching it').
21.root: ب-ل-غ (b-l-gh) — to reach, attain, arrive at

22.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
22.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

23.meaning: A noun meaning 'a call, a plea, an invocation, a prayer of entreaty'; the verbal act of calling upon Allah, asking and beseeching. It is a fuller, more drawn-out word for supplication than its shorter cousin.
23.grammar: A masculine singular verbal noun (naming the act of 'calling/supplicating'). The final -u ending is the nominative case, used when the noun is the subject of a sentence or the thing being described ('X is …').

24.meaning: The disbelievers / the ungrateful — those who reject faith and cover over the truth; the word also carries the sense of covering up or being ungrateful for what one has been given.
24.grammar: 'al-' is 'the'. The stem is an active participle ('one who disbelieves/is ungrateful') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the accusative/genitive form of the sound masculine plural: it marks the word as an object of a verb or as governed by a preposition, as opposed to the subject form -ūna.
24.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; ingratitude, disbelief

25.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
25.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

26.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
26.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

27.meaning: Means 'straying / error / being lost' — wandering off the right path, the opposite of guidance, whether literally losing one's way or going astray in belief and conduct.
27.grammar: An abstract noun: 'straying / error.' The -in ending is the genitive with 'tanwīn' (the -n marking it indefinite) — the case a noun takes after a preposition or in a possessive link, e.g. 'in an error.' The long -ā- belongs to this noun-pattern.
27.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray, lose the way

1.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and to Allah (belongs)' — expressing ownership or rightful belonging to Allah; the lām conveys possession or entitlement.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'wa-' ('and') joined to the prepositional phrase 'lillāhi'. This phrase is the preposition 'li-' ('to/for', here showing possession) prefixed to the name 'Allah'; when 'li-' attaches, the connecting hamza and the first lām of the definite article are elided in writing, leaving a single written lām for the preposition followed by the doubled (shadda-bearing) lām of the name. 'Allah' takes the -i (genitive) ending required after a preposition.

2.meaning: A present/future-tense verb meaning 'he/it prostrates, bows down in submission'; it denotes lowering oneself to the ground in worship and humble obedience — the deepest posture of submission before Allah.
2.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The final -u ending is the indicative mood, the plain-statement form used when no particle governs the verb to change its ending.
2.root: س-ج-د (s-j-d) — to prostrate, bow down in worship

3.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
3.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.
3.root: — (pronoun)

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

5.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
5.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

6.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
6.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.
6.root: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — earth, land

7.meaning: 'Willingly, obediently, of one's own accord' — acting out of voluntary compliance and submission rather than compulsion.
7.grammar: A noun used adverbially. The -an ending (with tanwīn, the 'n' sound) is the accusative, here describing the manner of an action — 'willingly, in a state of compliance.'

8.meaning: 'And unwillingly / by compulsion / reluctantly' — the opposite of willing obedience, doing something under force or against one's wishes.
8.grammar: The connector wa- ('and/or') prefixed to a noun used adverbially. The -an ending (accusative with tanwīn) shows the manner of an action — 'unwillingly, under duress.'
8.root: ك-ر-ه (k-r-h) — to dislike, find hateful; compulsion

9.meaning: A noun meaning 'their shadows / their shades' (plural). It refers to the shadows cast by things. The opening wa- means 'and', and the attached pronoun marks the shadows as belonging to 'them'.
9.grammar: A plural noun ('shadows') with the attached possessive pronoun -hum ('their'). The -u vowel before the pronoun is the nominative case, marking the word as a subject ('… and their shadows [do likewise]'). The doubled w- (wa-) reflects assimilation with the preceding sound.

10.meaning: 'In / at the morning(s).' Al-ghuduww denotes the early part of the day, the time of forenoon or morning — the period of setting out at daybreak. The prefixed bi- adds 'in', 'at', or 'during'.
10.grammar: A masculine noun made definite by al- ('the') and governed by the preposition bi- ('in / at'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which is the case a noun takes after a preposition such as bi-.

11.meaning: 'And in the evenings / late afternoons.' Al-āṣāl is the plural of aṣīl, the time of late afternoon stretching toward sunset — the closing part of the day. It is a natural counterpart to the morning hours.
11.grammar: A masculine broken (irregular) plural noun made definite by al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, here following from a governing preposition carried over earlier in the phrase. The prefixed wa- means 'and'.

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
2.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

3.meaning: A noun meaning 'Lord, Master, Sustainer'; it is a loaded term combining ownership, authority, and nurturing care — the one who creates, owns, governs, and brings a thing to its completion, providing for it at every step. When used of Allah it expresses His total lordship over all that exists.
3.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The final -u ending is the nominative case, used when the noun is the subject of a sentence or the predicate that describes it ('X is the Lord …').
3.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, own

4.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
4.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

5.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
5.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.

6.meaning: 'Say!' — a command to utter or declare something aloud, addressed to a single male.
6.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to one male: 'say!'. Its natural form ends in a silent consonant (qul), but here a short -i vowel is added simply to smooth pronunciation before a following word that begins with a connecting sound; it carries no case meaning of its own.
6.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, to speak

7.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
7.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

8.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
8.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.
8.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak

9.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'you (all) took / took up / adopted', here fronted by two question/connective particles giving the sense 'Have you then taken …?'. The verb conveys taking something for oneself, choosing or adopting it.
9.grammar: A perfect (past-tense) verb, second-person masculine plural, shown by the -tum ending ('you all did'). The -takhadh- stem is a Form VIII pattern meaning 'to take for oneself, adopt'. The leading a- is the interrogative particle ('?') and fa- means 'then/so', together forming a rhetorical question.
9.root: ا-خ-ذ (ʾ-kh-dh) — to take, seize, take hold of

10.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
10.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

11.meaning: Other than Him / apart from Him / besides Him. A relational word expressing the idea of being below, short of, or to the exclusion of something or someone.

parts.en: other than, apart from, besides, below

11.grammar: A relational noun/quasi-preposition meaning 'apart from / instead of'. It is followed by a possessive pronoun -hi ('Him'), which puts it in the genitive 'of' relationship; the kasra written under the pronoun reflects this genitive linkage.

12.meaning: Allies, protectors, intimate friends — those taken as close supporters, patrons, or guardians, with whom one stands in mutual loyalty (plural of walī).
12.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of 'walī.' Being a 'diptote' (a noun that resists the usual full set of endings), it takes a single final '-a' here for the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb or signals 'as / being' something — and notably without the usual '-n' (no nunation).

13.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
13.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

14.meaning: A present/future-tense verb meaning 'they own, possess, or have power/control over'; it conveys having mastery and the authority to dispose of something — to hold it in one's power, whether benefit or harm.
14.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'). The -ūna ending marks 'they (masculine plural)' in the indicative mood, the plain-statement form; it shortens to -ū when a governing particle precedes.
14.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to own, possess, have dominion

15.meaning: A phrase meaning 'for themselves / for their own selves'. The core noun means 'selves' or 'souls', the attached pronoun makes it 'their', and the prefix li- means 'for / belonging to'.
15.grammar: A plural noun ('selves') with the attached possessive pronoun -him ('their'), governed by the preposition li- ('for'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, required after a preposition; the pronoun appears as -him (rather than -hum) because it follows that -i vowel.

16.meaning: Benefit, profit, or advantage; something useful or gainful that brings good.
16.grammar: A singular noun marked indefinite ('benefit / some benefit'). The -an (tanwīn) combines the -a accusative case-ending — which typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) — with the -n of indefiniteness.

17.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
17.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

18.meaning: Harm / injury / hurt — that which damages or causes detriment; an affliction or adversity.
18.grammar: A noun. The final -an is 'nunation' (tanwīn) marking it as indefinite ('some harm / a harm'), and its -a vowel signals the accusative case — the ending typically used for the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon).
18.root: ض-ر-ر (ḍ-r-r) — harm, injury, damage, the opposite of benefit

19.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
19.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

20.meaning: An interrogative particle that turns a statement into a yes/no question, roughly "is it that…?" or "do…?". It can also carry a rhetorical or expectant tone rather than a literal request for information.
20.grammar: A question particle placed before a sentence to ask whether something is the case. It has no case ending and does not change form; it simply marks the words that follow as a yes/no question.

21.meaning: 'They are equal / it is the same' — to be on a par, level, or alike; to stand even with one another with no difference of value.
21.grammar: A Form VIII present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it is equal'). The 'ya-' prefix marks a present action; the weak final letter (from the root's last 'w/y') appears as the long ending. It expresses things being on the same level.

22.meaning: 'The blind one' — a person lacking sight. Often used figuratively for one who cannot perceive truth or guidance.
22.grammar: A definite descriptive noun/adjective ('the blind') marked by 'al-' ('the'), built on the pattern used for colours and bodily traits. It ends in a fixed long '-ā' vowel and does not change its ending for case — the form stays the same whether subject or object.
22.root: ع-م-ي (ʿ-m-y) — blindness, loss of sight or insight

23.meaning: A descriptive noun meaning 'the one who sees / the seeing one'; it denotes a being possessed of sight and, more deeply, of clear perception and insight. When used of Allah it affirms that He sees all things perfectly. The opening wa- means 'and'.
23.grammar: A definite noun/adjective (with al-, 'the') in an intensive pattern ('one who sees well, all-seeing'). The final -u ending is the nominative case, used when the word is a subject or the thing being described.

24.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', specifically the 'or' that pairs with a preceding question to offer an alternative ('…or…?'). It links two possibilities being weighed against each other, often after an opening interrogative.

parts.en: or (in alternatives, esp. after a question)

24.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case or tense ending). It typically introduces the second branch of a two-part question or a balanced alternative, presenting the two as equally consequential.

25.meaning: An interrogative particle that turns a statement into a yes/no question, roughly "is it that…?" or "do…?". It can also carry a rhetorical or expectant tone rather than a literal request for information.
25.grammar: A question particle placed before a sentence to ask whether something is the case. It has no case ending and does not change form; it simply marks the words that follow as a yes/no question.

26.meaning: A present/future-tense verb meaning 'they (two/things) are equal, level, or alike'; it conveys two things standing on a par, being even and equivalent — often used to ask or deny whether two things can ever be the same.
26.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb, third-person feminine singular, here agreeing with a feminine or plural subject ('they/it are equal'). The sta- element is a Form VIII/X pattern meaning 'to become even/equal'. The final -ī reflects the weak (yā') root letter; in the indicative the long vowel stands as the plain-statement form.
26.root: س-و-ي (s-w-y) — to be even, equal, level, balanced

27.meaning: A noun meaning 'the darknesses / the depths of darkness' (plural of 'darkness'). It denotes layers or kinds of darkness, and is often used figuratively for misguidance, ignorance, and disbelief as opposed to light.
27.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun (with al-, 'the'). The -āt is the sound feminine plural ending ('multiple darknesses'). The final -u marks the nominative case, used when the noun is a subject or the thing being described.

28.meaning: A noun meaning 'the light'; radiance and illumination, and figuratively guidance, faith, and truth that dispel darkness. The opening wa- means 'and'.
28.grammar: A definite masculine noun (with al-, 'the'; the l- assimilates into the following n-, giving an-nūr). The final -u ending is the nominative case, used when the noun is a subject or the thing being described.

29.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', specifically the 'or' that pairs with a preceding question to offer an alternative ('…or…?'). It links two possibilities being weighed against each other, often after an opening interrogative.

parts.en: or (in alternatives, esp. after a question)

29.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case or tense ending). It typically introduces the second branch of a two-part question or a balanced alternative, presenting the two as equally consequential.

30.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'they made, set up, appointed, or assigned'; a very broad verb of making — it can mean to create, to render something into a state, or to attribute/ascribe a thing to someone.
30.grammar: A perfect (past-tense) verb, third-person masculine plural ('they did'), shown by the -ū ending. The silent alif written after this -ū is a spelling convention and is not pronounced.
30.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, appoint, place

31.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
31.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

32.meaning: Associates, partners, or co-sharers — those set up as participants alongside another in ownership, authority, or worship. In theological usage it denotes rivals falsely placed beside Allah.
32.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of sharīk ('partner'), following the pattern faʿalāʾ. This pattern is a diptote, so it takes no nunation. The word is in the accusative case, marked by the short -a vowel on the word-final hamzah (آءَ); that hamzah is part of the plural pattern itself and cannot be split off as a separate ending. The accusative is the case typically used for the direct object of a verb ('they made/claimed partners') or after certain particles.

33.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'they created, brought into being, originated'; it denotes producing something new, shaping and forming it from nothing — a verb whose fullest sense belongs to the creative act of Allah.
33.grammar: A perfect (past-tense) verb, third-person masculine plural ('they did'), shown by the -ū ending. The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention and is not pronounced.
33.root: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q) — to create, bring into being, shape

34.meaning: A phrase meaning 'like His creating / like His creation'; the core noun names the act or product of creating, the attached pronoun makes it 'His', and the prefix ka- means 'like / as'.
34.grammar: A verbal noun ('creation/creating') with the attached possessive pronoun -hi ('His'), governed by the particle ka- ('like'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, required after ka-; the pronoun appears as -hi (rather than -hu) because it follows that -i vowel.
34.root: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q) — to create, bring into being, shape

35.meaning: It became similar/resembling, or grew confused through likeness — a Form VI verb conveying mutual resemblance, where things come to look alike or be hard to tell apart from one another. The fa- at the front marks a result or consequence ('and so', 'so that').
35.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in Form VI (tafāʿala), third-person masculine singular ('he/it did'). The final -a is the standard perfect ending. Form VI typically signals reciprocity or a state shared among parties — things resembling one another. The fa- prefix introduces a consequence following from what precedes.

36.meaning: The creating; the bringing of things into existence out of nothing, or the totality of what has been brought into being. As a noun it denotes both the act of fashioning/originating and, by extension, the created order itself.
36.grammar: A definite masculine singular noun. The final -u is the nominative case, which generally marks the word as the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified (the one doing or being something).
36.root: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q) — to create, originate, shape, bring into being

37.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
37.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
37.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

38.meaning: 'Say!' — a command to utter or declare something aloud, addressed to a single male.
38.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to one male: 'say!'. Its natural form ends in a silent consonant (qul), but here a short -i vowel is added simply to smooth pronunciation before a following word that begins with a connecting sound; it carries no case meaning of its own.

39.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
39.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

40.meaning: Creator, Originator, Maker — the one who brings things into existence and gives them their form. As a title of Allah it denotes the sole Author of all that exists.
40.grammar: An active participle ('one who creates') used as a noun. The final -u is the nominative ending, the case typically marking the subject of a sentence or a noun standing on its own. Often heads a possessive phrase ('Creator OF …').

41.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
41.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

42.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
42.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
42.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

43.meaning: And it / and he — a connective joined to the standalone pronoun 'he/it', often introducing a circumstantial clause ('while it…').
43.grammar: The prefix wa- ('and', or 'while' when introducing an accompanying circumstance) joined to the detached subject pronoun huwa, 'he/it' (masculine singular). The shadda on the wa- reflects assimilation of a preceding consonant onto it in connected speech. The pronoun is fixed in form and serves as the subject of its clause.

44.meaning: 'The One' — the single, unique, indivisible. As a divine name it points to Allah's absolute oneness, that there is nothing alongside Him and none like Him.
44.grammar: A definite noun/adjective ('the One'). The final -u ending is the nominative case, the form a word takes as the subject of a sentence or as a predicate describing it.
44.root: و-ح-د (w-ḥ-d) — to be one, single, unique

45.meaning: 'The Irresistible, the All-Subduer' — the One whose power overcomes and subdues everything, before whom all are compelled and nothing can resist. An intensive divine name.
45.grammar: A definite noun in an intensive pattern: the doubled middle radical (the hāʾ, marked by a shaddah) conveys overwhelming, habitual force — 'the One who utterly subdues'. The final -u ending is the nominative case, used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate.

1.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'he sent down, he caused to descend, he revealed' — used especially of Allah sending down revelation, rain, or blessings from above.
1.grammar: A completed (past) action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the -a ending marks third-person masculine singular. The form IV (causative) pattern means 'to make something come down,' i.e., to send it down.

2.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
2.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

3.meaning: The sky or heaven — the canopy overhead; the expanse above the earth, also that which is elevated or raised over something. With the definite article it means 'the sky / the heaven'.
3.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'), in the genitive marked by the -i ending. (The 'l' of al- assimilates in sound into the following 's', a 'sun letter', though it is still written.) The genitive -i ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').
3.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, loftiness; sky, heaven

4.meaning: 'water' — water in general, the fluid essential to life; also used for liquid such as rain. A basic noun for the substance of water.
4.grammar: An indefinite noun. The '-an' ending (tanwīn al-fatḥ) marks the accusative case together with indefiniteness — commonly the role of a direct object, the thing acted upon (e.g. what is sent down or brought).

5.meaning: And it flowed / streamed — to flow, as a liquid runs and pours along a course. The fa- prefix marks sequence or result ('and then', 'so').
5.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person feminine singular: the -t ending marks a feminine subject ('she/it flowed'). The fa- prefix links it as a consequence or next step in a sequence.

6.meaning: Valleys — the plural of wādī, a watercourse or low channel between hills through which water runs. The final -n (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('some valleys', 'valleys' in general).
6.grammar: A plural noun with the nominative case ending -un (indefinite nunation). The -u vowel typically marks the subject of a sentence ('the doer'), while the final -n signals that the noun is indefinite ('valleys', not 'the valleys').
6.root: و-د-ي (w-d-y) — valley, watercourse

7.meaning: By its measure / according to its capacity — the noun qadar ('measure, due proportion, capacity, decree') with the preposition bi- ('with/by') and an attached pronoun 'its/her'. It conveys that something happens to the extent it can hold or to its allotted amount.
7.grammar: A preposition bi- attached to a noun, followed by the possessive pronoun -hā ('its/her', feminine singular). The -i vowel on the noun is the genitive case, which is required after a preposition; the genitive also links the noun to the following possessor ('the measure OF it').

8.meaning: So it bore / carried up — a Form VIII verb meaning to carry, bear, or take up a load. The fa- prefix marks result or sequence ('and so', 'then').
8.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in Form VIII (iftaʿala), third-person masculine singular ('he/it carried'). The final -a is the perfect ending. Form VIII here gives the sense of taking up and bearing a load. The fa- prefix introduces a consequence.
8.root: ح-م-ل (ḥ-m-l) — carrying, bearing a load

9.meaning: The flood / torrent — rushing floodwater, a stream of water surging along. The al- prefix makes it definite ('the torrent').
9.grammar: A definite noun (with al-, the l assimilated into the sun-letter s). The final -u is the nominative case, which typically marks the noun as the subject — the one doing the action.

10.meaning: Foam / froth / scum — the worthless bubbly matter that rises and floats on the surface of flowing water or molten metal. The final -n (nunation) marks it as indefinite.
10.grammar: A noun with the accusative case ending -an (indefinite nunation). The -a vowel typically marks the noun as the object of a verb (the thing acted upon), and the final -n signals it is indefinite ('foam', not 'the foam').

11.meaning: Rising / swelling / floating high — an active participle ('the one that rises') from a verb meaning to swell up and mount upward, as foam that rides on the surface. The final -n (nunation) marks it as indefinite.
11.grammar: An active participle (the doer of the action, like English '-ing/-er' forms) with the accusative ending -an (indefinite nunation). The -a vowel marks the accusative — often the object or a descriptive complement — and the -n marks it indefinite. As a participle it describes something characterized by rising/swelling.

12.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and from/out of that which' or 'and from what'. It joins a new item to what precedes and points to an unspecified thing or category ('whatever it is that...').
12.grammar: A combination of the connector wa ('and'), the preposition min ('from, out of, part of'), and the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). The nūn of min has assimilated into the mīm of mā, doubling it (mim-mā). The whole phrase is invariable and does not take case endings.

13.meaning: They kindle / light a fire / heat up — a Form IV verb meaning to set ablaze or stoke a fire, here for melting or smelting. The ending shows a plural 'they' as the doers.
13.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb in Form IV (afʿala), third-person masculine plural. The -ūna ending means 'they (men/people) do' and marks an ongoing or habitual action. Form IV typically makes a verb causative — here, to cause fire to burn, i.e., to kindle.
