14.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
14.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

15.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
15.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

16.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
16.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').

17.meaning: Seeking, earnestly pursuing, desiring to attain — the act of going after something diligently. As a verbal noun it means 'a seeking / out of desire for.'

parts.en: seeking / earnest pursuit (the final -a is the accusative case ending, here expressing purpose/motive)

17.grammar: A verbal noun (the 'act of seeking') in the accusative case, shown by the final -a. In this role the accusative commonly expresses purpose or motive — 'out of a desire for / in seeking.' It is built on a Form VIII pattern conveying earnest, deliberate pursuit.
17.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to seek, desire, strive after something

18.meaning: Ornament / jewelry / adornment — decorative finery such as jewelry made of gold or silver. The final -n (nunation) marks it as indefinite.
18.grammar: A noun with the genitive case ending -in (indefinite nunation). The -i vowel marks the genitive, which typically follows a preposition or links to a preceding noun ('… of …'); the -n marks it indefinite.

19.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
19.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

20.meaning: Goods / wares / useful objects / enjoyment — anything one makes use of or benefits from: utensils, equipment, provisions, or the temporary enjoyments of life. The final -n (nunation) marks it as indefinite.
20.grammar: A noun with the genitive case ending -in (indefinite nunation). The -i vowel marks the genitive, which typically comes after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …'); the -n marks it indefinite.

21.meaning: Foam / froth / scum — the worthless bubbly matter rising to the surface of water or molten metal. The final -n (nunation) marks it as indefinite.
21.grammar: A noun with the nominative case ending -un (indefinite nunation). The -u vowel typically marks the noun as the subject (the doer or topic), and the -n marks it indefinite ('foam', not 'the foam').

22.meaning: 'Its like' / 'the like of it' — something equal or comparable to a previously mentioned thing.
22.grammar: A noun meaning 'like/equal' with the attached possessive pronoun -hu ('its/his'). The -u ending before the pronoun is nominative, the case used for a subject or predicate. The pronoun -hu refers back to a previously named masculine thing ('the like OF it').

23.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
23.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
23.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

24.meaning: He strikes / sets forth / coins — a verb whose core sense is 'to strike, beat', extended idiomatically to 'to set forth (a parable/example)', to 'travel/strike out over land', and more. The present-tense ya- prefix marks 'he/it' as the doer.
24.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it does'). The ya- prefix marks the 'he/it' subject; the final -u is the indicative ending, signaling a plain, ongoing, or habitual action (a simple statement of fact).
24.root: ض-ر-ب (ḍ-r-b) — striking, beating; by extension setting forth examples, traveling

25.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
25.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

26.meaning: The truth — that which is real, right, and established; reality, the just due, the genuine as opposed to the false.
26.grammar: A definite noun with 'the'. The -a ending is the accusative, typically marking the noun as the direct object of a verb ('the truth').
26.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, that which is established and real

27.meaning: And the false / vain / baseless — bāṭil denotes what is false, void, futile, and without truth or reality, the opposite of ḥaqq (truth). The wa- prefix means 'and'; al- makes it definite.
27.grammar: A definite noun (with al-) preceded by the conjunction wa- ('and'). It is an active participle in form ('that which is false/vain'). The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the object of a verb (the thing acted upon).

28.meaning: 'Then as for …' A connective opening that introduces and singles out a topic for comment, often paired later with a response. The fa- means 'then/so,' and 'ammā' sets up 'as for (such-and-such)…' to highlight one case among others.
28.grammar: A connector fa- ('then, so') joined to the detailing/conditional particle ammā ('as for…'). Ammā introduces a subject for separate treatment and normally anticipates a matching clause (often introduced by 'fa-') that gives the comment about it. Neither part takes case endings.

29.meaning: The foam / froth / scum — the worthless bubbly matter that floats on the surface. The al- prefix makes it definite ('the foam').
29.grammar: A definite noun (with al-, the l assimilated into the sun-letter z). The final -u is the nominative case, typically marking the noun as the subject — the topic or the doer of the action.

30.meaning: So it goes away / departs / vanishes — a verb meaning to go, depart, or pass off and disappear. The fa- prefix marks sequence or result ('and so', 'then').
30.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it goes'). The ya- prefix marks the 'he/it' subject; the final -u is the indicative ending, signaling a plain, ongoing, or habitual action. The fa- prefix introduces a consequence.

31.meaning: As discarded scum / cast-off jetsam / dross — that which is thrown aside and swept away, the useless residue left when something is jettisoned. The final -n (nunation) marks it as indefinite.
31.grammar: A noun with the accusative case ending -an (indefinite nunation). The -a vowel marks the accusative — here functioning as a descriptive complement (a 'state', i.e. 'as scum / in a discarded condition'); the -n marks it indefinite.

32.meaning: 'And as for …' A connective that introduces and sets apart a new topic for separate comment, usually anticipating a matching response clause. The 'and' joins it on; 'ammā' means 'as for (such-and-such)…'
32.grammar: The conjunction wa ('and') joined to the detailing/conditional particle ammā ('as for…'). Ammā singles out a topic for separate treatment and normally anticipates a matching clause (often introduced by 'fa-') that supplies the comment. Neither part takes case endings.

33.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
33.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

34.meaning: He/it benefits, profits, or brings advantage to someone; to be of use.
34.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he' or 'it'). The final -u ending is the indicative mood, used for a plain, ongoing or habitual statement of fact ('benefits / is benefiting').

35.meaning: Mankind, humanity, people in general — the collective of human beings.
35.grammar: A definite noun ('the people') with the attached 'al-' ('the'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (a sun letter), which is why the 'n' is doubled — this is a pronunciation effect, not a separate piece. The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the one being acted upon) or the subject of certain particles.
35.root: ن-و-س (n-w-s) — to move/sway; by extension, people

36.meaning: So it stays / remains / abides — a verb meaning to stay, tarry, and remain in place rather than passing away. The fa- prefix marks sequence or result ('and so', 'then').
36.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it stays'). The ya- prefix marks the 'he/it' subject; the final -u is the indicative ending, signaling a plain, ongoing, or habitual action. The fa- prefix introduces a consequence.

37.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
37.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

38.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
38.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

39.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
39.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
39.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

40.meaning: He strikes / sets forth / coins — a verb whose core sense is 'to strike, beat', extended idiomatically to 'to set forth (a parable/example)', to 'travel/strike out over land', and more. The present-tense ya- prefix marks 'he/it' as the doer.
40.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it does'). The ya- prefix marks the 'he/it' subject; the final -u is the indicative ending, signaling a plain, ongoing, or habitual action (a simple statement of fact).
40.root: ض-ر-ب (ḍ-r-b) — striking, beating; by extension setting forth examples, traveling

41.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
41.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

42.meaning: The likenesses / parables / examples — the plural of mathal, a comparison, similitude, or illustrative example used to make a truth vivid. The al- prefix makes it definite ('the examples').
42.grammar: A definite plural noun (with al-). The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the object of a verb (the thing acted upon).

1.meaning: A compound meaning 'for those who' or 'belonging to those who'. It joins the preposition 'for/to' with a masculine plural relative pronoun ('those who'), introducing a clause that describes a group of people by something they do or possess.
1.grammar: The prefix 'li-' is a preposition meaning 'for', 'to', or expressing ownership/benefit ('belonging to'). The relative pronoun is 'alladhīna' ('those who'), but when 'li-' attaches to it the connecting hamza of 'al-' drops out and the two lām sounds merge into one doubled lām, so the form is written and read 'lilladhīna' rather than 'li-alladhīna'. 'alladhīna' has a fixed shape and does not change for case.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'they answered / responded / complied'. The core sense is giving a favourable response to a call or request — to hearken and obey when summoned.
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb describing a completed action; it is built on a derived (augmented) pattern and on a hollow (weak-middle) root, so the middle root-letter surfaces as the long vowel -ā- of the stem rather than as a consonant. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they did…'). (The final silent alif is just a spelling convention after this plural -ū.)
2.root: ج-و-ب (j-w-b) — to answer, respond, reply (hollow/weak-middle root)

3.meaning: For/to their Lord — the noun rabb (the Lord: master, owner, sustainer, the One who nurtures and brings to completion) with the preposition li- ('for/to') and the pronoun 'their'. Rabb conveys ownership, authority, and continual nurturing care all at once.
3.grammar: A preposition li- ('for/to') attached to a noun, followed by the possessive pronoun -him ('their', masculine plural; vowelled -himu before a following word). The -i vowel on the noun is the genitive case, required after the preposition li-.
3.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, ownership, nurturing, sustaining

4.meaning: The best, the finest, the most beautiful (feminine form) — the supremely good outcome or reward; goodness in its highest degree.
4.grammar: A definite noun/adjective in the feminine superlative pattern ('the best, the finest'). Its long final 'ā' is a fixed ending that does not change for case; it denotes the utmost degree of goodness and often names the best reward or recompense.

5.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
5.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

6.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

6.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.
6.root: — (particle; no triliteral root)

7.meaning: They respond, answer, or comply with a call. From 'istajāba', to answer favourably, to respond to a request or invocation, to grant a response. In plural it means 'they answer / they comply'.
7.grammar: A present/imperfect verb in the Form X pattern (which here carries the sense of seeking or giving a response). The 'ya-...-ū' framing marks third-person masculine plural, 'they'. The '-ū' ending with no final 'n' shows the subjunctive or jussive mood, the form a verb takes after certain particles (such as a conditional or negating word) rather than as a plain statement.

8.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
8.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

9.meaning: A conditional particle introducing a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact supposition: 'if (it were the case that…)'. It typically presents a condition that is unfulfilled or merely imagined, often implying the result did not or would not happen.
9.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case ending). It signals a hypothetical 'if': it sets up a supposed condition whose consequence is then stated, frequently with the sense 'if X were so, then Y would be so' — often where X is contrary to fact.

10.meaning: An emphatic particle meaning 'that' (as in 'I know that...') or 'indeed/surely.' It introduces a statement and gives it certainty and emphasis, presenting what follows as an established fact.
10.grammar: An emphatic particle that introduces a noun-clause ('that...'). It puts the following noun into the accusative case and lends the whole statement a sense of certainty and assertion. It typically comes after verbs of knowing, saying, or informing.

11.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
11.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

12.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
12.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

13.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
13.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

14.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
14.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

15.meaning: A word meaning 'all together', 'all of them', or 'the whole lot' — emphasising that no one and nothing is left out of a group.
15.grammar: A noun meaning 'all/entirety' carrying the -an ending: accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite '-n'). This accusative form is typical of a word that comes alongside another to specify it as 'all of them, every one', describing the manner or extent.

16.meaning: "and the like of it / and its equal" — the noun "like, equal, counterpart" joined by "and" and carrying the attached pronoun "it," i.e., something matching or equal to it.
16.grammar: A masculine noun ("a like/equal") opened by the connector "and" and carrying the attached pronoun "-hu" ("it/its"). The stem vowel "-a" (mithla) is the accusative ending, typically marking it as the object of a verb or governed by a preceding word; the pronoun appears as "-hu" because the preceding vowel is "a."

17.meaning: Together with him; in his company or alongside him.
17.grammar: An adverb of accompaniment, 'with', joined to the attached pronoun -hu 'him'. Together they mean 'with him / in his company'.

18.meaning: They would surely offer it as ransom / would ransom themselves — a Form VIII verb meaning to give something as a ransom or redemption to free oneself. The la- prefix is an emphatic 'surely/certainly'.
18.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in Form VIII (iftaʿala), third-person masculine plural ('they did'); the -aw ending (the plural -ū fused with the weak final root letter) marks the 'they' subject. The la- prefix adds emphasis ('surely'), characteristically introducing the answer to a hypothetical 'if'.
18.root: ف-د-ي (f-d-y) — ransom, redemption, offering a price to free

19.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
19.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

20.meaning: 'those / those ones' — a demonstrative pointing to a group of people or things at a distance ('those there').
20.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those.' The -ka element adds the sense of pointing to something farther off (as opposed to 'these' near at hand). Being a fixed pronoun, it keeps one form regardless of case.

21.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
21.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

22.meaning: "evil / badness of" — that which is bad, harmful, or offensive; the wrongness or foulness of a thing. In the construct form it means 'the evil of …'.
22.grammar: A noun meaning 'evil/badness'. The final -u is the nominative case, the case used for a subject or for the thing being asserted. The bare (non-tanwīn) ending shows it is in a construct (possessive) chain, leaning on a following noun: 'the evil OF …'.
22.root: س-و-أ (s-w-') — to be bad, to harm, to do evil; that which displeases

23.meaning: The reckoning / accounting / settling of accounts — ḥisāb is the act of counting, calculating, and calling to account, especially the final taking-to-account of deeds. The al- prefix makes it definite ('the reckoning').
23.grammar: A definite noun (with al-). The final -i is the genitive case, which typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').
23.root: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b) — counting, calculating, reckoning, calling to account

24.meaning: And their place of return, their final abode — the dwelling to which they ultimately come back and where they will settle, combined with 'their'.
24.grammar: A noun of place ('a place to which one resorts') with an attached possessive pronoun. The prefix wa- means 'and'. The ending -hum is the attached pronoun 'their/them' for a masculine group, showing that the abode belongs to them. The noun's own ending is a fixed long -ā that does not change for case.
24.root: ء-و-ي (ʾ-w-y) — to take shelter, resort to, give refuge

25.meaning: Hell / Jahannam — the proper name of the Fire of punishment in the Hereafter.
25.grammar: A proper name (the name of Hell), treated as a feminine, non-fully-inflecting noun. The final -u is the nominative case ending, marking it as the subject/predicate of a statement ('… is Jahannam'). Because it is a proper name of this type, it does not take the usual final '-n' (tanwīn) of ordinary nouns.

26.meaning: And how evil / wretched (it is)! — wa joined to biʾsa, a fixed verb of blame used to condemn something as bad, the opposite of niʿma ('how excellent'). It expresses strong disapproval.
26.grammar: Conjunction wa- ('and') plus biʾsa, a frozen verb of blame ('how wretched is …') that does not change for tense. It introduces strong condemnation of whatever follows as its subject, the counterpart of niʿma ('how good is …').

27.meaning: The resting place / bed / couch — mihād is a spread-out, prepared place to lie or settle upon, like a bed or cradle made smooth and ready. The al- prefix makes it definite ('the resting place').
27.grammar: A definite noun (with al-). The final -u is the nominative case, which typically marks the noun as the subject or the topic being described.
27.root: م-ه-د (m-h-d) — spreading out, smoothing, preparing a bed/cradle

1.meaning: An interrogative formed from three pieces meaning roughly 'Is then the one who…?' It opens a rhetorical question that compares two parties. The 'a-' is a question marker, 'fa-' links to a preceding statement and means 'then/so', and 'man' is the relative pronoun 'the one who / whoever'.
1.grammar: A combination of particles plus the relative pronoun 'man'. The leading 'a-' turns the sentence into a yes/no question (often rhetorical). 'fa-' is a connective meaning 'then/so', tying the question to what came before. 'man' refers to a person and introduces a clause describing them ('the one who…'); it does not change its ending for case.

2.meaning: He knows / is knowing — a verb meaning to know, to have certain knowledge of something. The present-tense ya- prefix marks 'he/it' as the doer.
2.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it knows'). The ya- prefix marks the 'he/it' subject; the final -u is the indicative ending, signaling a plain, ongoing, or habitual fact.

3.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'that …' or 'only that' — it introduces and emphasizes a fact as the content of a thought or statement; 'anna' asserts ('indeed/that') and the attached 'mā' often gives a restrictive sense ('that … is only …').
3.grammar: A combination of the emphatic particle 'anna' ('that, indeed') with 'mā'. 'Anna' introduces a noun-clause as the object of verbs like 'think' or 'know', putting the following noun in the accusative. Joined with 'mā' it frequently carries a limiting force, 'only/merely'. Particles like this do not themselves take case endings.
3.root: — (particles; no triliteral root)

4.meaning: 'It was sent down / revealed': the act of being caused to descend, used especially of revelation brought down from Allah. The passive form puts the focus on the thing sent down rather than on the sender.
4.grammar: A past-tense passive verb in Form IV (anzala 'to send down' → unzila 'was sent down'). The prefix is only the u- vowel carried on the connecting hamza; the nūn that follows is the first root letter (of ن-ز-ل), not part of the prefix. The internal vowel pattern u–i marks it as passive ('was/were sent down'), with no named doer. The final -a marks the subject as 'he/it', a single masculine thing, and signals completed action.
4.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down; (Form IV) to send down

5.meaning: 'To you' (addressing one person): indicating direction or motion toward a single individual — that toward which something moves or is directed.
5.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, towards') with an attached pronoun; before a suffix ilā takes the form ilay-. The -ka ending is the pronoun 'you' for a single male addressee. Pronouns following a preposition stand in the genitive relationship, though their form does not visibly change for case.

6.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
6.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
6.root: — (preposition)

7.meaning: The Lord belonging to a single male 'you' — Rabb is the Master, Owner, and Sustainer who creates, nurtures, and brings to maturity; here 'your Lord'.
7.grammar: The noun rabb (Lord, Sustainer) with the attached pronoun -ka, 'your' for one male. The -i ending before the pronoun is genitive, the case that typically links a word to a following possessor or follows a preposition (here showing the possession 'of you'). The doubled b (shadda) belongs to the root.

8.meaning: 'The truth / the reality; what is right, real, and rightfully due.' A weighty noun meaning that which is firmly true and real, as opposed to falsehood; it also carries the senses of a rightful claim, a duty owed, and justice. With the article it denotes 'the Truth' in a definite, absolute sense.
8.grammar: A definite noun: the prefix al- ('the') plus the stem. The final -u ending is the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a word identifying what something is (as in 'X is the truth').
8.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, reality, rightness; that which is established and rightfully due

9.meaning: Means 'like one who …' — combines 'like / as' with 'the one who,' setting up a comparison to a person defined by what they do.
9.grammar: Two pieces: the prefix ka- means 'like / as' (a comparison particle that puts the following noun in the genitive), and 'man' is the relative pronoun 'who / the one who.' Together: 'like the one who …,' typically contrasting one party with another.

10.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
10.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

11.meaning: Lacking sight; one who cannot see. The word denotes a person or thing characterized by blindness, and is frequently used in a figurative sense for spiritual or moral blindness — an inability to perceive truth or guidance.
11.grammar: A noun/adjective on the intensive 'afʿal' pattern used for bodily traits, masculine singular. It denotes a permanent characteristic ('blind') rather than a passing state. Its final long 'ā' is fixed and does not change for the usual case-endings.

12.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
12.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

13.meaning: He takes heed, calls to mind, reflects and is reminded. The verb conveys an inward act of recollection that leads to heeding admonition — letting a reminder sink in and bear fruit in awareness.
13.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular, of the reflexive 'tafaʿʿala' pattern (originally yatadhakkaru, with assimilation), which adds an inward, self-directed force ('to remind oneself'). The 'ya-' prefix marks 'he/it'; the '-u' ending marks the plain indicative, i.e. an ongoing or habitual action ('does / keeps doing').

14.meaning: 'Possessors of / owners of / people of' — a plural construct word meaning those endowed with or characterized by whatever follows it (e.g. 'those of understanding'). It has no singular of its own form and is always joined to a following noun.
14.grammar: A masculine plural noun used only in the construct state (always followed by another noun, 'possessors OF ...'). The -ū ending is the nominative plural form, marking it as the subject or doer of a sentence. The trailing alif is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.
14.root: — (a word for 'possessors of', having no verbal root)

15.meaning: The kernels, cores, or innermost parts — figuratively the faculties of sound reason and understanding, the discerning intellect that grasps the heart of a matter. The prefixed "al-" makes it definite ("the").
15.grammar: A definite plural noun (singular "lubb"). The '-i' ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("… OF …") or follows a preposition. Here the genitive marks it as the thing possessed after a possessor-word.

1.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
1.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

2.meaning: They fulfil, discharge in full, and make good on something owed — carrying out a pledge or obligation completely and faithfully, without falling short.
2.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine plural, of the form-IV 'afʿala' pattern (which carries a causative/completive sense: 'to bring to fullness'). The 'ya-/yū-' element marks 'they', and the '-ūna' ending marks both masculine plural and the plain indicative ('they do / keep doing'); dropping the final 'na' would signal a different mood.
2.root: و-ف-ي (w-f-y) — fulfilment, completeness, paying in full

3.meaning: A noun phrase meaning 'with the covenant / pledge of …' — a solemn binding agreement, here in the construct state, meaning it is bound to a following word it belongs to (the covenant 'of' someone or something).
3.grammar: A noun preceded by the preposition bi- ('with / by'). The -i ending is genitive, required after the preposition; because the noun bears no nunation and no article, it is in construct ('the covenant OF …'), linking forward to a following possessor.
3.root: ع-ه-د (ʿ-h-d) — covenant, pledge, binding agreement, charge

4.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
4.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

5.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
5.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

6.meaning: A verb meaning 'they break', 'they undo', or 'they violate' — to undo or dissolve something firmly tied, especially to break a pledge, covenant, or binding agreement.
6.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'). The ya- prefix marks third person and the -ūna ending marks a masculine-plural subject in the indicative mood (ongoing or habitual action). The core sense is the undoing of something firmly bound, such as a covenant.
6.root: ن-ق-ض (n-q-ḍ) — to break, undo, unravel (a pact)

7.meaning: A solemn covenant, pact, or binding agreement; a firmly ratified compact entered into with pledged commitment.
7.grammar: A definite singular noun (the 'al-' prefix means 'the') on the 'mifʿāl' pattern, which names an instrument or weighty thing — here a firmly bound compact. The '-a' ending is accusative, the case that typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon).

1.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

2.meaning: They (plural) join / connect / reach — they attach themselves to something or arrive at it; also used of maintaining ties and bonds of kinship.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine plural ('they …'). The ending -ūna marks the plural 'they' and the indicative mood (a plain statement of an ongoing or habitual action).
2.root: و-ص-ل (w-ṣ-l) — to join, connect, reach, maintain ties

3.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
3.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'he commanded', 'he ordered', or 'he enjoined' — to issue an authoritative instruction that something be done.
4.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The bare three-letter stem ending in -a denotes a completed action by a single male subject: 'he gave a command'. It commonly takes a person commanded and a thing commanded.

5.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
5.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

6.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
6.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

7.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
7.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

8.meaning: A verb meaning 'that it be joined' or 'to be connected' — the passive of joining or linking one thing to another so that it is united or maintained.
8.grammar: Present/imperfect verb in the passive voice, third-person masculine singular ('it is joined'), in the basic (form I) pattern, in the subjunctive mood marked by the final -a. The yu- prefix with the passive vowelling means the subject receives the action rather than doing it ('be joined'). The subjunctive -a typically appears after particles meaning 'that' or 'to', expressing a dependent or purposed action.
8.root: و-ص-ل (w-ṣ-l) — to join, connect, link, maintain ties

9.meaning: And they stand in awe, reverence, and fear — a fear mingled with reverence and a keen sense of accountability, especially before what is sacred or before the consequences of wrongdoing.
9.grammar: The prefix 'wa' means 'and'. The core is a present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine plural, with 'ya-' marking 'they'. Because the root ends in a weak letter, the plural shows as '-aw-na'; the '-na' ending marks masculine plural in the plain indicative ('they do'). The root denotes a reverential dread rather than mere fright.
9.root: خ-ش-ي (kh-sh-y) — reverent awe, dread mixed with reverence

10.meaning: Their Lord, Master, and Sustainer — 'rabb' is the one who owns, nurtures, and brings a thing to its full development; with the attached pronoun, the Lord who is theirs.
10.grammar: A masculine noun with the possessive 'their' attached. The -a vowel before -hum marks the accusative case, the case typically used for the object of a verb.

11.meaning: And they are afraid, dread, and apprehend harm. The verb expresses ordinary fear of something threatening or of an undesirable outcome.
11.grammar: The prefix 'wa' means 'and'. The core is a present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine plural, from a hollow root (middle weak letter, surfacing as the long 'ā'). The 'ya-' element marks 'they', and the '-ūna' ending marks masculine plural in the plain indicative ('they do / keep doing').

12.meaning: Evil, badness, or harm; that which is bad or grievous. As a construct noun it points to the 'evil of' or 'badness of' whatever follows.
12.grammar: A masculine singular noun on the 'fuʿl' pattern meaning 'evil/badness'. The '-a' ending is accusative — the case for a direct object, and also the case a noun takes as the first term of a possessive ('X-of') construction leading into a following genitive noun.
12.root: س-و-أ (s-w-ʾ) — evil, badness, that which grieves or harms

13.meaning: The reckoning, accounting, or calling to account — the tallying and settling of deeds; also calculation or counting in a general sense.
13.grammar: A definite verbal noun with the article 'al-' ('the'). The final -i (kasra) marks the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or as the second part of a possessive pair ('… of the reckoning').

1.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

2.meaning: 'They were patient / they endured steadfastly / they persevered.' The verb means to restrain oneself, to bear hardship with calm endurance, to hold firm and not give way to panic or complaint. Ṣabr is steadfast, self-controlled perseverance.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb (Form I) in the masculine plural 'they' person. The stem ṣabar- carries the completed-action (past) sense. The -ū ending marks the doers as 'they' (masculine plural) who performed the act ('they were patient / they endured'). The written alif after it is a silent spelling convention that regularly follows the plural -ū on a verb and is not pronounced.

3.meaning: Seeking, earnestly pursuing, desiring to attain — the act of going after something diligently. As a verbal noun it means 'a seeking / out of desire for.'

parts.en: seeking / earnest pursuit (the final -a is the accusative case ending, here expressing purpose/motive)

3.grammar: A verbal noun (the 'act of seeking') in the accusative case, shown by the final -a. In this role the accusative commonly expresses purpose or motive — 'out of a desire for / in seeking.' It is built on a Form VIII pattern conveying earnest, deliberate pursuit.
3.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to seek, desire, strive after something

4.meaning: Face — the front of the head; by extension, what is turned toward something, hence one's presence, favour, or the goal/object aimed at (as in seeking the 'face' of someone, meaning their pleasure or sake).
4.grammar: A masculine singular noun ('face'). The -i ending is the genitive case, which typically either follows a preposition or links the word to a following noun in a possessive 'of' relationship (e.g. 'the face OF …').
4.root: و-ج-ه (w-j-h) — face, to turn toward, direction

5.meaning: 'Their Lord' — the base 'rabb' means Lord, Master, Sustainer: the one who owns, nurtures, governs, and brings to maturity. As a divine title it conveys Allah as Creator and Sustainer of all.
5.grammar: The noun 'rabb' ('Lord, Sustainer') with the attached pronoun '-him' ('their'). The '-i' before the pronoun is the genitive case, the form used after a preposition or, as in a possessive linkage, to show belonging ('of/their').
5.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain; lordship

6.meaning: And they established / set up and kept up — they put a thing firmly in place and maintained it duly. Often used of upholding prayer, i.e. performing it properly and consistently.
6.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and'. The stem is a past-tense verb on a causative pattern (Form IV, 'to make stand, to set up and keep up'); the -ū ending is the subject 'they' (masculine plural), marking a completed action they performed.
6.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; (causative) to set up, uphold

7.meaning: The ritual prayer (ṣalāh): the prescribed formal worship of standing, bowing, and prostrating before Allah at appointed times. As a verbal noun it also carries the underlying sense of calling upon, supplicating, and blessing.
7.grammar: A definite feminine noun. The -a ending is accusative: it generally marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon, e.g. that which is established or performed), or the object of certain particles.

8.meaning: And they spent or laid out — to disburse wealth, expending it (especially in giving and charitable outlay).
8.grammar: A past-tense verb (form IV) prefixed with 'wa' (and). The suffix '-ū' is the subject ending for a third-person masculine plural — 'they (did it)' — marking a completed action carried out by a group.
8.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — spending, expending, disbursing wealth

9.meaning: From what / from that which — a fusion of the preposition 'from' with the relative 'what/which', introducing the thing or situation being referred to.
9.grammar: A merger of 'min' ('from') and 'mā' ('what/that which'); the 'n' of 'min' assimilates into the 'm' of 'mā', doubling it. The combination means 'from what ...' and typically introduces a following clause describing the thing referred to. Being particles, neither part takes a case ending.

10.meaning: 'We provided/bestowed upon them': the act of granting sustenance and provision — food, wealth, and every good thing a creature lives on — given to a group of people. The verb conveys provision freely supplied by a giver.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -nā suffix is the subject 'we' (a past-tense form meaning the action is completed). The attached -hum is the object pronoun 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group). So the structure is 'we + [verb] + them'.
10.root: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — to provide, to grant sustenance/provision

11.meaning: 'Secretly / in secret' — privately, in a hidden manner; also can mean a secret matter itself.
11.grammar: A noun used adverbially. The ending -an is the indefinite accusative (tanwīn fatḥ); in the accusative an indefinite noun like this commonly functions as an adverb of manner ('secretly').

12.meaning: And openly / in public — a verbal noun meaning open display or doing something in the open where others can see, as opposed to secretly; joined with 'and.'
12.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') plus a verbal noun meaning 'openness, public display.' The final -tan (the feminine ending pronounced with -an) is the indefinite accusative, working adverbially — describing the manner of an action ('openly, in public'). Indefinite means 'in an open way' rather than 'the.'
12.root: ع-ل-ن (ʿ-l-n) — to be open, public, made known

13.meaning: And they ward off, repel, push back, or avert — turning something away or driving it back, as one fends off harm or counters a wrong.
13.grammar: The prefix 'wa' means 'and' (written with doubled 'w' through assimilation to a preceding word). The core is a present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine plural; 'ya-' marks 'they', and the '-ūna' ending marks masculine plural in the plain indicative ('they do / keep doing').

14.meaning: 'With / for the good deed' — the noun ḥasana (a good deed, a fine thing, a benefit) made definite ('the') and governed by the preposition bi- ('with/for/by'). It denotes a beautiful or beneficial act or reward.
14.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the prefixed preposition bi- ('with/for') and the article al- ('the'). The final -i marks the genitive case, which is required after a preposition. The feminine -a(t) ending is built into the word.

15.meaning: The bad deed, the evil act, the wrong; an offense or misdeed. It can also denote a misfortune or calamity that befalls — anything bad, viewed as a single instance.
15.grammar: A definite singular noun (the 'al-' prefix means 'the'); it is feminine, marked by the closed 'ta' (-a/-at) ending, and functions as the noun-form of 'something bad'. The final '-a' is accusative, the case that typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon).

16.meaning: 'those / those ones' — a demonstrative pointing to a group of people or things at a distance ('those there').
16.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those.' The -ka element adds the sense of pointing to something farther off (as opposed to 'these' near at hand). Being a fixed pronoun, it keeps one form regardless of case.

17.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
17.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

18.meaning: The outcome, final result, or end-consequence of a matter; what ultimately comes after and follows from something — its sequel or final reward.
18.grammar: A feminine singular noun on the 'fuʿlā' pattern, denoting the end-result or aftermath of a course of action. Its final long 'ā' is fixed and does not change for the usual case-endings; as the first term of a possessive construction it conveys 'the outcome of …'.
18.root: ع-ق-ب (ʿ-q-b) — following after, succession, consequence, end-result

19.meaning: A noun meaning 'the abode' or 'the home' — a dwelling place. It frequently denotes a final, lasting abode (such as the eternal home of the Hereafter), as opposed to a temporary lodging.
19.grammar: A definite noun ('the abode') marked by the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The final '-i' ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('the … OF the abode') or follows a preposition. The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the 'd', doubling it (al-dār → ad-dār).
19.root: د-و-ر (d-w-r) — to turn, to encircle; a dwelling, abode

1.meaning: Gardens — lush, densely shaded enclosures whose foliage covers the ground; the plural of the word for a garden, used pre-eminently for the Gardens of Paradise.
1.grammar: A feminine sound plural of 'janna' (garden), formed with the '-āt' plural ending. The final '-u' is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a noun that simply names or identifies something ('… are gardens').
1.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — covering, concealing; lush garden whose growth covers the earth

2.meaning: Perpetual residence, lasting settlement — an abode of permanence and enduring stay; classically a proper name for the Gardens of eternal dwelling.
2.grammar: A verbal noun used as a name for a place of permanent dwelling. The ending -in is the genitive case with nunation (tanwīn): the -i vowel typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …') or follows a preposition, while the final -n signals that it is indefinite.

3.meaning: They enter it / they will enter it. The verb expresses going in or passing into a place, with an attached object meaning 'it' (a feminine thing or place).
3.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine plural ('ya-' = 'they'), with the '-ūna' indicative ending (here written '-ū-na-hā'). The attached '-hā' is an object pronoun meaning 'it/her/them (feminine)', so the whole means 'they enter it'. The plain indicative signals an ongoing or future action.
3.root: د-خ-ل (d-kh-l) — entering, going in, penetrating

4.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
4.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

5.meaning: He was righteous, sound, upright, and in good order; he did right and was fit and wholesome. The verb describes being or becoming good and setting things aright.
5.grammar: A past/perfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular. The bare stem with the final '-a' marks completed action by 'he' ('he was/became righteous'). The root conveys soundness, integrity, and being fit and in good order — the opposite of corruption.
5.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — soundness, righteousness, setting right, wholesomeness

6.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
6.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
6.root: — (preposition)

7.meaning: 'Their fathers / their forefathers' — male ancestors and forebears, with the attached pronoun 'their'.
7.grammar: An irregular ('broken') plural of 'ab' ('father') with the attached pronoun '-him' ('their', referring to males). The '-i' before the suffix is genitive — used after a preposition or to link to a preceding noun ('… of …') — and the pronoun is '-him' rather than '-hum' because of it.

8.meaning: And their spouses / their mates. The base word denotes a pair-member — a spouse, partner, or one of a matched pair — with an attached pronoun meaning 'their'.
8.grammar: The prefix 'wa' means 'and'. 'Azwāj' is the broken plural of 'zawj' (spouse/one of a pair). The '-i' ending is genitive — the case taken after a preposition, in a possessive ('… of …') construction, and before an attached possessor pronoun; the suffix '-him' means 'their' (and its 'i' vowel reflects that genitive setting).
8.root: ز-و-ج (z-w-j) — pairing, coupling, spouse, one of a matched pair

9.meaning: 'And their descendants / their offspring' — the lines of progeny issuing from people, plural, with the attached pronoun 'their'.
9.grammar: The sound feminine plural of 'dhurriyya' ('offspring'), prefixed with 'wa' ('and') and carrying the pronoun '-him' ('their'). The '-i' before the suffix marks the genitive (after a preposition or linking to a preceding noun); for the sound feminine plural this same '-i' also serves as the accusative ending.
9.root: ذ-ر-ر / ذ-ر-أ (dh-r-r / dh-r-ʾ) — to scatter, to multiply (offspring); progeny

10.meaning: And the angels — pure, created beings of light who serve and obey Allah; 'malāʾikah' is the plural of 'malak', an angel.
10.grammar: A plural noun 'angels' made definite by 'al-' ('the') and preceded by 'wa' ('and'). The '-at-' is the feminine-form plural marker, and the final -u ending is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence.
10.root: أ-ل-ك (ʾ-l-k) — sending, conveying a message (an angel as a bearer of a message); the noun is also linked to م-ل-ك (m-l-k), dominion/ownership

11.meaning: 'they enter' — to go into or pass inside a place.
11.grammar: A present/future verb, 3rd-person masculine plural ('they …'). The ending -ūna combines the plural 'they' (-ū) with the indicative marker -na, signalling a simple ongoing or future statement. The ya- prefix marks the third person.
11.root: د-خ-ل (d-kh-l) — to enter, go in, penetrate

12.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
12.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
12.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

13.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
13.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

14.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
14.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

15.meaning: A gate or doorway — an opening through which one enters, here a single one and indefinite ('a gate').
15.grammar: A common noun. The -in ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a gate') and in the genitive case, the case typically used after a preposition or after another noun in a possessive link ('...of a gate').

1.meaning: Peace, soundness, safety, well-being — freedom from harm and discord; a word of greeting and of the wholeness and security that comes from being safe and at peace.
1.grammar: A noun. The ending -un is the indefinite nominative: the -u marks the nominative (the form a subject or a stated/announced word takes), and the final -n ('tanwīn') marks it as indefinite ('peace', not 'the peace').

2.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
2.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

3.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
3.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.
3.root: — (particle + relative pronoun)

4.meaning: You endured patiently, you bore steadfastly, you persevered. The verb denotes patient endurance and self-restraint in the face of hardship, addressed to a group of people.
4.grammar: A past/perfect verb with the subject built into the ending: '-tum' marks completed action by 'you' (masculine plural, addressing more than two people) — 'you (all) endured/persevered'. The root carries the sense of holding firm, restraining oneself, and bearing trials without giving way.

5.meaning: How excellent! / What a fine thing is …! A fixed expression of praise meaning that the thing named is excellent and goodly — declaring something to be best or most fitting.
5.grammar: The prefix 'fa-' means 'so / and then', linking to what precedes. 'Niʿma' is a frozen verb of praise — it does not conjugate for tense in the ordinary way and is used to extol whatever noun follows as excellent ('how good is …!'). Its counterpart for blame is 'biʾsa' ('how evil is …!').
5.root: ن-ع-م (n-ʿ-m) — goodness, favour, that which is excellent and pleasing

6.meaning: The outcome, final result, or end-consequence of a matter; what ultimately comes after and follows from something — its sequel or final reward.
6.grammar: A feminine singular noun on the 'fuʿlā' pattern, denoting the end-result or aftermath of a course of action. Its final long 'ā' is fixed and does not change for the usual case-endings; as the first term of a possessive construction it conveys 'the outcome of …'.
6.root: ع-ق-ب (ʿ-q-b) — following after, succession, consequence, end-result

7.meaning: A noun meaning 'the abode' or 'the home' — a dwelling place. It frequently denotes a final, lasting abode (such as the eternal home of the Hereafter), as opposed to a temporary lodging.
7.grammar: A definite noun ('the abode') marked by the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The final '-i' ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('the … OF the abode') or follows a preposition. The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the 'd', doubling it (al-dār → ad-dār).
7.root: د-و-ر (d-w-r) — to turn, to encircle; a dwelling, abode

1.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'they break', 'they undo', or 'they violate' — to undo or dissolve something firmly tied, especially to break a pledge, covenant, or binding agreement.
2.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'). The ya- prefix marks third person and the -ūna ending marks a masculine-plural subject in the indicative mood (ongoing or habitual action). The core sense is the undoing of something firmly bound, such as a covenant.
2.root: ن-ق-ض (n-q-ḍ) — to break, undo, unravel (a pact)

3.meaning: A noun meaning 'covenant', 'pledge', or 'binding promise' — a solemn, sacred commitment or pact, especially one entered into with Allah.
3.grammar: Singular noun in the accusative case, marked by the final -a. The accusative ending here typically signals that the noun is the object of a verb. In a construct chain it would also be the first ('possessed') term linking to a following noun ('the covenant OF …').
3.root: ع-ه-د (ʿ-h-d) — to pledge, make a covenant, commit

4.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
4.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

6.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'after' — the time or position following something; 'afterward', 'following'.
6.grammar: An adverb of time functioning as a noun, here in the genitive case marked by the final -i. The genitive ending typically appears after a preposition or as the second term of a construct ('after THE …'), linking 'after' to a following noun to specify what it comes after.
6.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — to be after, to follow, distance in place or time

7.meaning: Its covenant / the covenant of it. The base word is a solemn, firmly ratified pact, with an attached pronoun meaning 'it/his', linking the covenant to its owner or maker.
7.grammar: A singular noun on the 'mifʿāl' pattern (naming a weighty, binding thing). The '-i' ending is genitive — the case used after a preposition, in a possessive ('… of …') construction, and before an attached possessor pronoun; the suffix '-hi' means 'its/his' (its 'i' vowel matching the genitive setting), giving 'its covenant'.

8.meaning: A verb meaning 'and they cut off' or 'and they sever' — to cut, sever, or break apart a connection, joined to the connective 'and'.
8.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), preceded by the connective wa- ('and'). The ya- prefix marks third person and the -ūna ending marks a masculine-plural subject in the indicative mood (ongoing or habitual action). The wa- joins it to a preceding clause.
8.root: ق-ط-ع (q-ṭ-ʿ) — to cut, sever, cut off

9.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
9.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

10.meaning: A verb meaning 'he commanded', 'he ordered', or 'he enjoined' — to issue an authoritative instruction that something be done.
10.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The bare three-letter stem ending in -a denotes a completed action by a single male subject: 'he gave a command'. It commonly takes a person commanded and a thing commanded.

11.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
11.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

12.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
12.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

13.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
13.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

14.meaning: A verb meaning 'that it be joined' or 'to be connected' — the passive of joining or linking one thing to another so that it is united or maintained.
14.grammar: Present/imperfect verb in the passive voice, third-person masculine singular ('it is joined'), in the basic (form I) pattern, in the subjunctive mood marked by the final -a. The yu- prefix with the passive vowelling means the subject receives the action rather than doing it ('be joined'). The subjunctive -a typically appears after particles meaning 'that' or 'to', expressing a dependent or purposed action.
14.root: و-ص-ل (w-ṣ-l) — to join, connect, link, maintain ties

15.meaning: A verb meaning 'and they spread corruption' or 'and they cause ruin' — to work mischief, ruin, or disorder in the world, joined to the connective 'and'.
15.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), in the causative (form IV) pattern, preceded by the connective wa- ('and'). The yu- prefix with the causative vowel and the -ūna ending mark a masculine-plural subject in the indicative mood. The form-IV pattern gives the sense of actively bringing about corruption or ruin.
15.root: ف-س-د (f-s-d) — to be corrupt, spoil, cause disorder

16.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
16.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

17.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
17.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

18.meaning: 'those / those ones' — a demonstrative pointing to a group of people or things at a distance ('those there').
18.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those.' The -ka element adds the sense of pointing to something farther off (as opposed to 'these' near at hand). Being a fixed pronoun, it keeps one form regardless of case.

19.meaning: To them / for them — the preposition li- ('to, for') joined to the pronoun 'them'. It expresses that something is directed toward, belongs to, or is for the benefit of a group.
19.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') combined with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). When li- takes a pronoun its vowel becomes 'la-'. The final -u here is a connecting vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word; it carries no case meaning of its own.

20.meaning: The curse — being cast out and removed from mercy, divine rejection and condemnation; the calling-down of expulsion from good upon someone.
20.grammar: A definite singular noun (the 'al-' prefix means 'the'); it is feminine, marked by the closed 'ta' (-a/-at) ending. The final '-u' is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a noun that simply names or identifies something ('… is the curse').
20.root: ل-ع-ن (l-ʿ-n) — cursing, driving away, banishment from mercy

21.meaning: 'And for them / and they have.' A combination expressing possession or entitlement belonging to a group of males: 'and to/for them (belongs).' The particle li- conveys 'for' or 'belonging to,' and the attached pronoun refers to 'them.'
21.grammar: A possessive/benefactive phrase: the preposition li- ('for, belonging to') with the attached object pronoun -hum ('them,' masculine plural). Such 'for X' phrases commonly express that something belongs to or is owed to that party.

22.meaning: "evil / badness of" — that which is bad, harmful, or offensive; the wrongness or foulness of a thing. In the construct form it means 'the evil of …'.
22.grammar: A noun meaning 'evil/badness'. The final -u is the nominative case, the case used for a subject or for the thing being asserted. The bare (non-tanwīn) ending shows it is in a construct (possessive) chain, leaning on a following noun: 'the evil OF …'.
22.root: س-و-أ (s-w-') — to be bad, to harm, to do evil; that which displeases

23.meaning: A noun meaning 'the abode' or 'the home' — a dwelling place. It frequently denotes a final, lasting abode (such as the eternal home of the Hereafter), as opposed to a temporary lodging.
23.grammar: A definite noun ('the abode') marked by the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The final '-i' ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('the … OF the abode') or follows a preposition. The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the 'd', doubling it (al-dār → ad-dār).
23.root: د-و-ر (d-w-r) — to turn, to encircle; a dwelling, abode

1.meaning: Allah — the proper name of the One God, the sole and absolute Deity worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a name, not a common noun, and refers to the Creator and Sustainer of all that exists.
1.grammar: The proper divine name. The final -u ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject (the doer) of a sentence or the noun being identified.

2.meaning: He spreads out, extends, stretches forth, and makes ample. The verb conveys laying something open and wide, and so giving abundantly or enlarging a provision.
2.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular; the 'ya-' prefix marks 'he/it', and the final '-u' marks the plain indicative — an ongoing or habitual action ('he extends / keeps extending'). The root pictures spreading a thing out flat and wide, hence giving generously.
2.root: ب-س-ط (b-s-ṭ) — spreading out, extending, expanding, making ample

3.meaning: The provision; sustenance, livelihood, and the means of life — whatever bounty is granted to support and nourish a creature, whether food, wealth, or any good thing bestowed.
3.grammar: A definite singular noun (the 'al-' prefix means 'the'; its 'r' doubles the sun-letter assimilation of the 'l'). It is a verbal noun on the 'fiʿl' pattern denoting that which is provided. The final '-a' is accusative, the case that typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing given or acted upon).
3.root: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — provision, sustenance, bestowing the means of life

4.meaning: 'for whoever / to the one who' — the preposition 'for/to' joined with the relative word 'who', introducing the person(s) about whom something is said.
4.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') combined with the relative/interrogative word 'man' ('who, whoever'). Together they single out a person or group as the focus ('for the one(s) who...').

5.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
5.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
5.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

6.meaning: And He measures out, restricts, straitens, or apportions sparingly; to set a fixed measure to provision so as to limit it. The same verb can also mean to have power and to determine.
6.grammar: The prefix 'wa' means 'and'. The core is a present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular; 'ya-' marks 'he/it', and the final '-u' marks the plain indicative — an ongoing or habitual action ('he restricts / keeps measuring out'). The root joins the ideas of measuring, decreeing, and having power.
6.root: ق-د-ر (q-d-r) — measuring, apportioning, determining, power

7.meaning: And they rejoiced, were glad, exulted. The verb denotes feeling joy and delight; depending on context it ranges from wholesome gladness to giddy, self-satisfied exultation.
7.grammar: The prefix 'wa' means 'and'. The core is a past/perfect verb, 3rd person masculine plural; the '-ū' ending (written with a silent trailing 'alif') marks completed action by 'they' — 'they rejoiced'. The root denotes the rising of joy and gladness in the heart.

8.meaning: "with / by the life" — the noun ḥayāh (life, living existence) made definite and governed by the preposition 'with/in'.
8.grammar: A definite noun governed by the preposition bi- ('with/in/by'). Because a preposition precedes it, the noun is in the genitive case, shown by the -i ending (here -ti on the tā' marbūṭa). The article al- makes it 'the life', and bi- links it as 'with the life'.
8.root: ح-ي-ي / ح-ي-و (ḥ-y-y/w) — to live, be alive; life

9.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
9.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
9.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

10.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
10.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

11.meaning: 'The life' — earthly existence, the span of living in this world. The word denotes life as the state of being alive, vitality, and the worldly life as a whole.
11.grammar: 'al-' is the definite article 'the'. The final '-u' is the nominative ending, which typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence (the one doing or being something), or as the predicate naming what something is.

12.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
12.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
12.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world
