13.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
13.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

14.meaning: The Hereafter — the final, lasting life that comes after death and the present world; literally 'the last/latter (abode or life)', as opposed to the first, nearer life.
14.grammar: A feminine adjective used as a noun, with 'the'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …'), or follows a preposition or oath particle.
14.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after, end

15.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
15.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

16.meaning: An enjoyment, a passing benefit, provision for temporary use; goods or comforts one makes use of for a while. The word often carries the sense of something fleeting compared with what lasts.
16.grammar: A masculine singular noun on the 'mafʿāl' pattern, denoting a thing enjoyed or used. The final '-un' (tanwīn) marks both the nominative case (subject or simple naming, '… is an enjoyment') and indefiniteness ('a / an' — some enjoyment, not a specific one).
16.root: م-ت-ع (m-t-ʿ) — enjoyment, benefit, provision for temporary use

1.meaning: And he says, and he will say. A verb of speaking covering plain statement, and by extension holding an opinion or asking.
1.grammar: A present-tense verb for a single male ('he says/will say'), joined by wa- ('and'). The ya- prefix marks the third-person masculine singular subject. The final -u is the indicative ending, signalling a plain statement of fact (ongoing or future) rather than a command or a 'so that' clause.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
3.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

4.meaning: A particle of urging or exhortation meaning 'why not …?' — used to press for or demand that something be done, and sometimes to express a wish, often with a tone of reproach ('why does … not happen?').
4.grammar: An indivisible particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). Although written as one form, it is not built up from the conditional 'if' plus a negation; in this prompting usage it is a single fixed particle meaning 'why not?' / 'if only.' Followed by a verb it presses for that action. (Note: in a different construction the same form can mean 'were it not for,' but that is a separate usage.) It is a particle and takes no case ending.

5.meaning: 'It was sent down / revealed': the act of being caused to descend, used especially of revelation brought down from Allah. The passive form puts the focus on the thing sent down rather than on the sender.
5.grammar: A past-tense passive verb in Form IV (anzala 'to send down' → unzila 'was sent down'). The prefix is only the u- vowel carried on the connecting hamza; the nūn that follows is the first root letter (of ن-ز-ل), not part of the prefix. The internal vowel pattern u–i marks it as passive ('was/were sent down'), with no named doer. The final -a marks the subject as 'he/it', a single masculine thing, and signals completed action.
5.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down; (Form IV) to send down

6.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
6.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

7.meaning: A sign, token, or mark — and especially a 'verse' of revelation. It denotes a clear indicator that points to a deeper truth: a miracle, a proof, or a portion of revealed text.
7.grammar: A feminine noun in the nominative case with tanwīn (the -un ending), marking it as indefinite ('a sign') and typically the subject or doer of a sentence. The nominative shows it is acting or being identified rather than acted upon.

8.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
8.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

9.meaning: A phrase meaning 'his Lord'. 'Lord' (rabb) denotes the Master, Owner, Sustainer, and Nurturer who creates, provides for, and governs — far richer than a mere title; here joined to 'his'.
9.grammar: The noun 'Lord' with the genitive -i ending followed by the attached pronoun -hi ('his'). The genitive case appears because the noun is linked to a preceding word ('… OF his Lord') or follows a preposition. The lengthened -hī reflects how this pronoun is pronounced after an -i vowel.
9.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing, ownership, sustaining and bringing to completion

10.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
10.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

11.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
11.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

12.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
12.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

13.meaning: A verb meaning 'he leads astray' or 'he lets go astray' — to cause someone to lose the right way, to misguide or allow to wander from the correct path.
13.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'), in the causative (form IV) pattern. The yu- prefix marks third-person singular with the vowel typical of derived causative verbs, and the final -u marks the indicative mood (ongoing or habitual action). The causative pattern gives the sense of 'causing to go astray'.
13.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray, err

14.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
14.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

15.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
15.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
15.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

16.meaning: 'And he/it guides, leads rightly, directs to the way' — a verb for showing the right path and leading someone toward correct guidance.
16.grammar: An imperfect (present/ongoing) verb from a weak-final root, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks the masculine singular subject and the stem ends in a long ī; the prefixed wa- means 'and'.
16.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, leading to the right way

17.meaning: 'To Him' or 'toward Him' — the preposition expressing direction or endpoint ('to / toward') combined with a pronoun referring to a single masculine person, indicating motion or attention directed at him.
17.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base 'ilā shifts to 'ilay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -hi is the third-person masculine singular object of a preposition, 'him'; its -i vowel is the form the pronoun takes after the 'ay' sound.

18.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
18.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

19.meaning: He turned back (in repentance), returned, and turned to attentively. The verb expresses turning oneself back toward something — characteristically a contrite turning to one's Lord again and again.
19.grammar: A past/perfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular, of the form-IV 'afʿala' pattern (from a hollow root, with the middle weak letter surfacing as the long 'ā'). The final '-a' marks completed action by 'he' ('he turned back'). The pattern conveys deliberately directing oneself back toward something.
19.root: ن-و-ب (n-w-b) — returning, turning back repeatedly, recourse

1.meaning: Those who / the ones who — a plural relative pronoun (masculine) introducing a description: 'those (people) who …'.
1.grammar: A relative pronoun, masculine plural, meaning 'those who / the ones who'. It refers back to a group already in view and introduces a clause describing them. Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
2.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

3.meaning: And it becomes calm, tranquil, and reassured; it settles into a state of secure, untroubled rest. Used of a heart that ceases its agitation and comes to ease and quiet confidence.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb in the third-person feminine singular ('she/it'), the feminine matching grammatically feminine subjects. The closing -u ending marks the indicative mood: the plain, factual statement of an action ongoing or habitual. The wa- prefix is the connector 'and'.
3.root: ط-م-ن (ṭ-m-n) — calm, tranquility, reassurance of heart

4.meaning: 'Their hearts' — the hearts belonging to a masculine plural group. In Qur'anic usage the 'heart' is the seat of understanding, intention, feeling, and faith, not merely the physical organ.
4.grammar: A plural noun ('hearts') in the nominative, shown by the -u before the pronoun, which typically marks it as the subject of a sentence. The attached 'hum' means 'their' (a group of males or mixed group), giving 'their hearts.'
4.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart; to turn over, fluctuate

5.meaning: By means of the remembrance, mention, or calling-to-mind of something; the act of keeping a thing present in thought and on the tongue, often the remembrance of Allah.
5.grammar: A preposition bi- ('with, by, through') attached to a noun. The -i ending is genitive, which is what a noun takes after a preposition; it also links the noun to a following noun in an 'X of Y' relationship.

6.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
6.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

7.meaning: An opening particle of alert and emphasis — 'Now then!', 'Beware!', 'Truly!'. It calls attention to and strongly affirms the statement that follows.
7.grammar: An attention-drawing particle placed at the start of a statement. It rouses the listener and emphasizes what comes next, somewhat like 'Indeed!', 'Lo!', or 'Take note!' in English.

8.meaning: By means of the remembrance, mention, or calling-to-mind of something; the act of keeping a thing present in thought and on the tongue, often the remembrance of Allah.
8.grammar: A preposition bi- ('with, by, through') attached to a noun. The -i ending is genitive, which is what a noun takes after a preposition; it also links the noun to a following noun in an 'X of Y' relationship.
8.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — remembrance, mention, recollection

9.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
9.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

10.meaning: It becomes calm, tranquil, and reassured; it settles into secure, untroubled rest. Used of a heart that ceases its agitation and finds ease and quiet confidence.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb in the third-person feminine singular ('she/it'), the feminine matching grammatically feminine subjects. The closing -u ending marks the indicative mood: a plain, factual statement of an action ongoing or habitual.
10.root: ط-م-ن (ṭ-m-n) — calm, tranquility, reassurance of heart

11.meaning: The hearts — the inner seats of feeling, understanding, intention, and faith. In Arabic the heart (qalb) is the core of the person where conviction and emotion reside, not merely the organ.
11.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun, 'hearts', made definite by the prefix al- ('the'). The -u ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject or doer of a sentence — the one performing or undergoing the action.
11.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart, turning, the inmost core

1.meaning: Those who / the ones who — a plural relative pronoun (masculine) introducing a description: 'those (people) who …'.
1.grammar: A relative pronoun, masculine plural, meaning 'those who / the ones who'. It refers back to a group already in view and introduces a clause describing them. Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
2.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

3.meaning: A two-part word: 'and' + 'they did / worked / performed.' The verb denotes doing deeds, working, putting effort into action — practical doing as opposed to mere speaking or believing.
3.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' + a past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they' (a group of males or a mixed group): 'and they did / worked.'
3.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act

4.meaning: 'The righteous deeds / good works' — the definite plural of a word meaning that which is sound, wholesome, upright, and beneficial. As a noun it refers to good, virtuous actions that set things right.
4.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun ('the good deeds'). The -i ending is the oblique case used by feminine plurals to mark either the genitive ('… of …' / after a preposition) or the accusative (direct object); for this plural pattern the accusative and genitive share the same -i ending.
4.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, good, upright, set right

5.meaning: A state of supreme goodness, blessedness, and felicity; well-being and a happy final outcome. Often understood as a name for ultimate bliss or for a tree in Paradise, conveying 'all good be theirs.'
5.grammar: A noun built on a pattern conveying intensity and abundance of good. It ends in a final long vowel ā (written as a 'restrained' alif), so its case is not marked by a short vowel; the word stays fixed in form.
5.root: ط-ي-ب (ṭ-y-b) — goodness, pleasantness, that which is wholesome and pure

6.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
6.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

7.meaning: And the goodness, beauty, or excellence of something; that which is fine, fair, and pleasing. The noun names the quality of being good or beautiful.
7.grammar: A noun, 'goodness/beauty', with the connector wa- ('and') prefixed. The -u ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject; in a possessive phrase it carries the 'X of Y' meaning ('the beauty of …'), the following noun being its complement.

8.meaning: A place or point of return; the destination to which one ultimately comes back, and by extension one's final resort or homecoming.
8.grammar: A noun of place built on the ma- pattern, denoting where an action happens — here 'place of return.' The ending -in is genitive with nunation (the -n sound marking an indefinite noun, 'a place of return'); the genitive is the case taken after another noun or a preposition.
8.root: أ-و-ب (ʾ-w-b) — returning, coming back, turning back

1.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
1.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
1.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

2.meaning: 'We sent you / We dispatched you' — the act of sending forth one male addressee, as one is sent on a mission or as a messenger.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb on the form-IV ('afʿala') pattern (to send), with two attached pronouns: 'nā' is the subject 'we,' and the final 'ka' is the object 'you' (one male). So it states a completed act, 'we sent you.'

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
3.root: — (particle)

4.meaning: A community, nation, or people — a body of people bound together by shared faith, way of life, or origin; one collective group.
4.grammar: A feminine noun. The final -in (genitive with 'nunation') marks it as indefinite ('a community') and links it to a preceding noun or preposition ('… of a community'). The feminine -t sound surfaces before the ending.

5.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
5.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

6.meaning: 'It passed away / went by, came to an end' — said of a community, time, or era that has elapsed and is now gone. The root carries the sense of being emptied out, hence of time or people that have passed.
6.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -t (sukūn-marked -at) suffix marks a third-person feminine singular subject, 'she/it,' used here because the noun it refers to is grammatically feminine. The past tense states a completed action.
6.root: خ-ل-و (kh-l-w) — to be empty/vacant; to pass away, elapse

7.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
7.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

8.meaning: Before it; the time or position prior to a (feminine) thing already mentioned. Marks what comes earlier in sequence or precedence.
8.grammar: The time-word qabl ('before') with the attached pronoun -hā ('it/her', referring to a feminine noun). The -i ending is genitive, the case this word takes as an adverb of place/time governing the pronoun that follows.
8.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — before, precedence, that which comes prior

9.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'communities / nations / peoples' — groups of beings bound together as distinct collectives, each a community in its own right.
9.grammar: An indefinite plural noun (plural of 'umma', a community or nation). The -un ending (tanwīn) marks indefiniteness ('communities') together with the nominative case — the naming form used for a subject or predicate. The final '-n' sound is pronounced but not written as a letter.
9.root: أ-م-م (ʾ-m-m) — community, nation; a way/path followed in common

10.meaning: So that you may recite, read aloud, or follow in succession; to convey a text by reading it out, with the sense of following one part after another.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb, second-person singular ('you'), governed by the purpose particle li- ('so that, in order to'). After this particle the verb takes the subjunctive: the final ending shifts to -a (here written tatluwā with the weak final letter), expressing intended or hoped-for action ('that you recite') rather than a plain fact.
10.root: ت-ل-و (t-l-w) — recitation, reading aloud, following in sequence

11.meaning: 'Upon them / against them' — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, against') carrying an attached plural pronoun referring to a group of males.
11.grammar: ʿalā ('upon') takes the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The -him ending is the attached pronoun for a masculine plural 'them'; its final vowel appears as -u (himu) to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with the definite article.

12.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
12.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

13.meaning: 'We revealed / inspired' — the act of God conveying revelation or inspiration; to communicate a message swiftly and privately into someone's heart or to a prophet. Here attributed to 'we'.
13.grammar: A past-tense verb in a causative pattern (to convey/send down a revelation). The suffix -nā marks the doer as 'we', giving 'we revealed'. As past tense, it reports a completed act.
13.root: و-ح-ي (w-ḥ-y) — to reveal, to inspire, to convey swiftly and secretly

14.meaning: 'To you' (addressing one person): indicating direction or motion toward a single individual — that toward which something moves or is directed.
14.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, towards') with an attached pronoun; before a suffix ilā takes the form ilay-. The -ka ending is the pronoun 'you' for a single male addressee. Pronouns following a preposition stand in the genitive relationship, though their form does not visibly change for case.

15.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
15.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

16.meaning: 'They disbelieve / reject faith', or more literally 'they cover over (the truth), they are ungrateful'. An ongoing or habitual rejection and denial.
16.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a masculine plural 'they' acting now or habitually; the final -na (kept, not dropped) shows the verb is in its plain indicative form, stating an ongoing fact.
16.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — covering over; hence disbelief and ingratitude

17.meaning: By the All-Merciful — al-Raḥmān, a name of Allah denoting boundless, all-embracing mercy that overflows to the whole of creation; a quality so intense it functions almost as a proper name.
17.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with, by, in') joined to the definite name al-Raḥmān. The -i ending is genitive, the case a noun takes after a preposition. The name follows an intensive pattern signifying mercy that is vast, overflowing, and all-encompassing.

18.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
18.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

19.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
19.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

20.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
20.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
20.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

21.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
21.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

22.meaning: God / object of worship — a deity that is worshipped. The bare noun names the concept of a worshipped god.
22.grammar: A singular noun carrying an -a ending. This short -a typically marks the accusative (object) case; it is also the form a noun takes immediately after the absolute-negation particle 'lā' to mean 'no … (at all).'
22.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, worship, being a deity

23.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
23.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

24.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
24.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

25.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
25.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

26.meaning: I placed my trust, I relied wholly — to commit one's affairs entirely to another and depend on Him, resting in reliance. The verb's intensive pattern conveys deliberate, complete entrusting.
26.grammar: A past-tense verb in a reflexive intensive pattern (carrying the sense of taking something fully upon oneself — 'to entrust oneself, rely'). The -tu ending means the doer is 'I' and the action is completed.
26.root: و-ك-ل (w-k-l) — to entrust, appoint as guardian, rely upon

27.meaning: And to Him / toward Him. The wa- means 'and'; ilā is the preposition 'to/toward' indicating direction or destination; the attached pronoun -hi means 'him'.
27.grammar: Wa- means 'and'. Ilā ('to/toward') is a preposition of direction; it takes the special form 'ilay-' before a pronoun. The attached -hi is the genitive pronoun 'him', the form pronouns take after prepositions; the -i vowel reflects that genitive attachment.

28.meaning: My turning-back in repentance; my return to Allah. The noun names the act of repenting and returning, with the attached 'my' making it personal.
28.grammar: A verbal noun on the ma- pattern, 'a turning-back / repentance', with an attached possessive 'my' (the final -i that replaces the case-marking and means 'my'). So the word reads 'my repentance / my returning.'
28.root: ت-و-ب (t-w-b) — repentance, turning back to Allah

1.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
1.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').

2.meaning: An emphatic particle meaning 'that' (as in 'I know that...') or 'indeed/surely.' It introduces a statement and gives it certainty and emphasis, presenting what follows as an established fact.
2.grammar: An emphatic particle that introduces a noun-clause ('that...'). It puts the following noun into the accusative case and lends the whole statement a sense of certainty and assertion. It typically comes after verbs of knowing, saying, or informing.

3.meaning: A recitation, a reading; a text meant to be recited aloud. As a common noun it denotes 'something recited,' and as a proper name it is the Qur'an, the recited Scripture.
3.grammar: A verbal noun meaning 'recitation.' The ending -an is accusative with nunation (the -n marking it indefinite, 'a recitation'); the accusative is the case typically marking the object of a verb or a noun being specified.
3.root: ق-ر-أ (q-r-ʾ) — reading, reciting aloud

4.meaning: It was set in motion and made to move along, caused to travel or be driven onward. A passive sense: the thing did not move itself but was moved by another.
4.grammar: A past-tense passive verb in an intensive form, third-person feminine singular. The inner vowels (u–i) mark it passive — 'it was made to move' rather than 'it moved.' The suffix -t signals a feminine subject, and the intensive form adds force or repetition to the action.

5.meaning: By it, with it, through it; the preposition 'bi' (with/by means of) joined to a pronoun referring to something previously mentioned.
5.grammar: A preposition plus an attached third-person masculine singular pronoun ('it / him'). 'Bi' conveys instrument or means ('by means of it'); the pronoun takes the -i vowel because words governed by 'bi' stand in the genitive.

6.meaning: The mountains — the great, firmly rooted masses of rock and earth, often evoked as images of immovable solidity.
6.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun, 'mountains', made definite by al- ('the'). The -u ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject or doer — the one the sentence is about.
6.root: ج-ب-ل (j-b-l) — mountain, that which is firmly fixed

7.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
7.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

8.meaning: It was cut up, severed, and torn apart into pieces; thoroughly broken open or rent asunder. A passive sense with an intensive force of repeated, complete cutting.
8.grammar: A past-tense passive verb in an intensive form, third-person feminine singular. The inner vowels (u–i) mark it passive — 'it was cut' rather than 'it cut.' The intensive form conveys thorough, repeated cutting ('cut to pieces'), and the suffix -t signals a feminine subject.
8.root: ق-ط-ع (q-ṭ-ʿ) — cutting, severing, breaking apart

9.meaning: By it, with it, through it; the preposition 'bi' (with/by means of) joined to a pronoun referring to something previously mentioned.
9.grammar: A preposition plus an attached third-person masculine singular pronoun ('it / him'). 'Bi' conveys instrument or means ('by means of it'); the pronoun takes the -i vowel because words governed by 'bi' stand in the genitive.

10.meaning: A noun meaning 'the earth', 'the ground', or 'the land' — the terrestrial world, the soil and land surface as opposed to the sky.
10.grammar: A noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The -u ending is nominative, which typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence (the one doing the action). This noun is grammatically feminine.

11.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
11.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

12.meaning: It was spoken to, addressed in speech, made to be talked with. A passive sense: speech was directed toward it by another.
12.grammar: A past-tense passive verb in an intensive form, third-person masculine singular. The inner vowels (u–i) mark it passive — 'it was addressed' rather than 'it spoke.' The intensive form here carries the sense of being directly and fully addressed with words.

13.meaning: By it, with it, through it; the preposition 'bi' (with/by means of) joined to a pronoun referring to something previously mentioned.
13.grammar: A preposition plus an attached third-person masculine singular pronoun ('it / him'). 'Bi' conveys instrument or means ('by means of it'); the pronoun takes the -i vowel because words governed by 'bi' stand in the genitive.

14.meaning: 'The dead' — those who have died or are without life; the lifeless, as a group.
14.grammar: A definite plural noun/adjective ('the dead'). It is of a plural pattern that ends in a fixed long -ā, so its ending does not change with grammatical position; it refers collectively to those who are dead.

15.meaning: A particle of retraction and transition meaning 'rather,' 'on the contrary,' or 'nay.' It cancels or sets aside what was just said and corrects course toward a truer statement that follows — turning the listener from one idea to another.
15.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it never changes its ending). It functions to retract or override the preceding statement and introduce a correction or contrast — 'no, rather …'

16.meaning: A combination 'to/for Allah / belonging to Allah' — the preposition 'to/for' joined to the name Allah, expressing that something is due to, owned by, or directed toward Allah.
16.grammar: The prefix li- is the preposition 'to / for / belonging to'. 'Allah' follows, with the initial alif of 'Allāh' elided after li-. The final -i is the genitive ending required after a preposition; it marks Allah as the One to whom something belongs or is directed.

17.meaning: The matter, affair, or command; a thing decided upon or ordered, or a situation/business at hand. It can denote both a "command" and an "affair" depending on usage.
17.grammar: A definite noun with prefixed al- ("the"). The -u ending is nominative: it typically marks the word as a subject or as the thing an action is predicated of.

18.meaning: A word meaning 'all together', 'all of them', or 'the whole lot' — emphasising that no one and nothing is left out of a group.
18.grammar: A noun meaning 'all/entirety' carrying the -an ending: accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite '-n'). This accusative form is typical of a word that comes alongside another to specify it as 'all of them, every one', describing the manner or extent.

19.meaning: "so have they then not…?" — a clustered opener combining 'so/then' with a questioning 'have they not?'; it poses a rebuking or prompting question about something that has not yet happened, urging reflection.
19.grammar: Three particles fused together: the questioning a- ('?'), the connective fa- ('so/then'), and lam, which negates and pushes a following present-tense verb into the meaning 'has/did not (do)'. Together they introduce a pointed rhetorical question about a past or completed matter.

20.meaning: He despairs, gives up hope; or, in a recognized usage, he comes to know with certainty. The verb conveys arriving at a settled inner conclusion — either abandoning hope or attaining sure knowledge.
20.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'), with the prefix ya- marking 'he.' The final -i here is a vowel taken after a vowelless letter or in pause, in place of the plain indicative ending; the verb expresses an ongoing or potential state.
20.root: ي-أ-س (y-ʾ-s) — despair, loss of hope; (idiomatically) certain knowledge

21.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
21.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

22.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
22.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

23.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
23.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

24.meaning: If — a conditional particle introducing a hypothetical that is contrary to fact or unfulfilled ("if [such-and-such had been the case]…"), typically implying that because the condition did not hold, its result did not occur either.
24.grammar: A conditional particle. It has no ending to inflect. It sets up a supposed condition, classically one understood as unreal or unrealized, and is normally answered by a result clause (often introduced by la-, "surely [then]…").

25.meaning: "He wills / wishes / desires" — denotes an act of will or volition, the choosing of something. As an ongoing/present-tense verb it expresses willing as a continuous, sovereign act.
25.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in the 'he' form. The ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular ('he'). The final -u ending is the indicative mood, marking a plain, ongoing statement of fact ('he wills').

26.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
26.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

27.meaning: He would surely have guided; emphatic statement that guidance would certainly have been given. To guide is to direct onto the right way and lead to the goal.
27.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he guided'), with the emphatic prefix la- ('surely, certainly') that strengthens the statement — often answering a 'had it been…' condition. The verb ends in a final long vowel (the weak final letter), so no short case-vowel appears.
27.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, showing the way, leading aright

28.meaning: Mankind, humanity, people in general — the collective of human beings.
28.grammar: A definite noun ('the people') with the attached 'al-' ('the'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (a sun letter), which is why the 'n' is doubled — this is a pronunciation effect, not a separate piece. The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the one being acted upon) or the subject of certain particles.
28.root: ن-و-س (n-w-s) — to move/sway; by extension, people

29.meaning: A word meaning 'all together', 'all of them', or 'the whole lot' — emphasising that no one and nothing is left out of a group.
29.grammar: A noun meaning 'all/entirety' carrying the -an ending: accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite '-n'). This accusative form is typical of a word that comes alongside another to specify it as 'all of them, every one', describing the manner or extent.

30.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
30.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

31.meaning: A verb meaning 'to cease / to stop being'. In negative constructions ('does not cease…') it conveys continuity — that something keeps on being the case.
31.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it ceases'). The 'ya-' prefix marks 'he/it', and the final '-u' is the ending used when the verb stands in its plain indefinite (indicative) state, expressing ongoing or general action. This is one of the 'sisters of kāna', typically paired with a negation to mean 'keeps on / still is'.
31.root: ز-و-ل (z-w-l) — to cease, depart, pass away

32.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
32.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

33.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
33.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
33.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

34.meaning: It strikes them, befalls them, reaches and hits them — used of a calamity or affliction that lands upon people.
34.grammar: A present-tense verb in the third-person feminine singular ('she/it', matching a feminine subject), with the attached object pronoun -hum ('them'). The verb is built on a causative form meaning 'to make something reach/hit a target,' and it expresses an action ongoing or habitual.
34.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — hitting the mark, befalling, reaching a target

35.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
35.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

36.meaning: They made, did, fashioned, or wrought. From 'ṣanaʿa', to make or craft something, to produce by skill or effort, to do a deed. In the plural completed form it means 'they made / they did / they produced'.
36.grammar: A past-tense (completed-action) verb. The '-ū' ending (with the silent written alif after it) marks third-person masculine plural, 'they (did)'. So it reports a completed action by a group: 'they made / they did'.
36.root: ص-ن-ع (ṣ-n-ʿ) — to make, fashion, craft, do

37.meaning: A striking calamity, a sudden crushing disaster; literally something that knocks or pounds. A blow of catastrophe that strikes with force.
37.grammar: An active participle used as a noun, feminine in form, 'a striking/pounding (thing).' The ending -un is nominative with nunation (the -n marking it indefinite, 'a calamity'); the nominative is the case typically marking the subject of a sentence.

38.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
38.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

39.meaning: It comes down and alights; it settles, descends upon, or takes up lodging at a place. Also carries the sense of an event befalling and landing on someone.
39.grammar: A present-tense verb in the third-person feminine singular ('she/it', matching a feminine subject). The closing -u ending marks the indicative mood: a plain, factual statement of an action ongoing or habitual.
39.root: ح-ل-ل (ḥ-l-l) — alighting, settling down, descending upon

40.meaning: An adjective meaning 'near, close, close at hand' — describing something short in distance, time, or relationship, easily reached or soon to come.
40.grammar: A masculine singular adjective on the 'faʿīl' pattern ('near, close'). The ending -an is the accusative case with tanwīn (nunation), which typically marks the word as agreeing with an accusative noun it describes, or otherwise governed into the accusative; the tanwīn shows it is indefinite.

41.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
41.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

42.meaning: Their home / dwelling — a dwelling-place or abode belonging to 'them'. Combines the noun 'home' with the possessor 'their'.
42.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -i ending is genitive — here triggered because the word follows a preposition or links to another noun. The suffix -him means 'their' (referring to a group of males); its 'i' vowel is the form taken after a genitive -i.
42.root: د-و-ر (d-w-r) — to turn/encircle; hence 'dār', an enclosed dwelling or abode

43.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
43.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.

44.meaning: He/it comes, brings, or arrives — to come or to bring (something) about. The form points to an action not yet completed (present or future).
44.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it comes'). The ya- prefix (a single, undoubled yāʾ) marks a single male/thing subject. The final -a (in -iya) is the subjunctive ending, which appears after certain particles meaning 'that', 'until', or 'so that', giving the sense '… that he come' or '… until he comes'.

45.meaning: The promise, pledge, or appointed assurance; a binding undertaking that something will come to pass — whether a good thing promised or a threatened outcome.
45.grammar: A verbal noun, 'a promise/pledge.' The -u ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject; in a possessive phrase it also carries the 'X of Y' sense ('the promise of …'), the following noun completing it.
45.root: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — promising, pledging, an appointed assurance

46.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
46.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

47.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
47.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

48.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
48.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

49.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
49.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

50.meaning: He breaks / fails to keep (a promise); He goes back on or leaves unfulfilled. From a verb whose core sense is 'to come after / be left behind', in this form meaning to default on a pledge or fail to deliver what was promised.
50.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The yu- prefix marks the doer as 'he' (third-person masculine singular) and, in this vowel pattern, indicates a causative-type form. The final -u is the indicative ending, which marks the plain factual present ('he does / will do'), as opposed to moods that drop or change that vowel.
50.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to come after, succeed, be behind; hence to break a promise (leave it behind unfulfilled)

51.meaning: The appointment / the appointed promise or time; a fixed tryst — a settled commitment as to when (or where) something will occur. It names the promised meeting or deadline itself.
51.grammar: A definite noun (with 'the') on a pattern denoting the time, place, or instrument of an action — here the appointed time/promise. The final -a is the accusative ending, generally marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
51.root: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — to promise, to appoint a time

1.meaning: A combination of three emphatic particles meaning roughly 'and most certainly indeed' — used to open a statement with strong, solemn affirmation that what follows is firmly established and true.
1.grammar: Particles, not a declinable word. 'wa' joins to what precedes; 'la-' is an emphatic prefix stressing certainty; 'qad' before a past-tense verb confirms the action definitely happened. Its final vowel appears as -i here only to ease pronunciation before a following consonant cluster (it carries no case meaning).

2.meaning: 'It/he was mocked / ridiculed / held in derision.' The passive of istahzaʾa — to make a mockery of someone, to deride or scoff at them.
2.grammar: A passive past-tense verb of Form X (the ista- pattern, here in its passive shape us-tu-…-i-a), third-person masculine singular, meaning 'he/it was mocked.' The passive is shown by the vowel pattern, and the bare -a ending names no agent — the focus is on the one mocked, not the mocker.
2.root: ه-ز-أ (h-z-ʾ) — to mock, ridicule, scoff, deride

3.meaning: 'Messengers' — those sent by Allah bearing a divine message to humankind; envoys commissioned to deliver revelation. This is the plural of rasūl.

parts.en: with / at (here governing the object of mockery)

3.grammar: A plural indefinite noun governed by the preposition bi-, which places it in the genitive case; the final -in (tanwīn kasr) is that indefinite genitive ending, the form a noun takes after a preposition or as a possessor.
3.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a messenger, an envoy

4.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
4.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

5.meaning: 'Before you' (in time or place): the period or position prior to a single person — that which comes earlier or stands in front, relative to one addressee.
5.grammar: The adverb/noun qabl ('before, prior') with the attached pronoun -ka ('you', a single male). The -i ending on qabl is genitive, the case regularly taken after a preposition (such as min, 'from before') and when a noun is linked to a following possessor; here it is linked to the pronoun 'you' ('before-you').
5.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, be before; priority, what comes first

6.meaning: So I granted a respite and let (them) be for a while; I gave time and delay, holding back from immediate action. Often used of deferring a reckoning so that someone is left to continue for a stretch.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb in a causative form, with the connector fa- ('so, then') prefixed. The suffix -tu marks the doer as first-person singular ('I'). The form conveys actively giving extension of time or delay to another.
6.root: م-ل-و / م-ل-ي (m-l-w / m-l-y) — granting respite, extending time, prolonging

7.meaning: A compound meaning 'for those who' or 'belonging to those who'. It joins the preposition 'for/to' with a masculine plural relative pronoun ('those who'), introducing a clause that describes a group of people by something they do or possess.
7.grammar: The prefix 'li-' is a preposition meaning 'for', 'to', or expressing ownership/benefit ('belonging to'). The relative pronoun is 'alladhīna' ('those who'), but when 'li-' attaches to it the connecting hamza of 'al-' drops out and the two lām sounds merge into one doubled lām, so the form is written and read 'lilladhīna' rather than 'li-alladhīna'. 'alladhīna' has a fixed shape and does not change for case.

8.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
8.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

9.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
9.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

10.meaning: I seized them, took hold of them with force; I caught and gripped them — frequently used of seizing wrongdoers for punishment.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb with two suffixes: -tu marks the doer as first-person singular ('I'), and -hum is the object 'them.' So the word reads 'I seized them,' the action completed in the past.

11.meaning: So how? / Then in what manner or state? — kayfa is the interrogative 'how', asking after the manner, condition or circumstance of something. With the prefixed 'so/then' it introduces a question following from what precedes, often expressing wonder or warning.
11.grammar: An interrogative particle ('how') carrying the connective prefix fa- ('so / then'), which links it to a preceding statement as a consequence or follow-up. As a particle, kayfa is indeclinable: its fixed final -a is not a case ending and does not change.

12.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

12.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

13.meaning: Penalty, punishment, or the painful retribution that follows wrongdoing; the consequence inflicted upon one who has done evil. With the attached 'my', it conveys a punishment belonging to or issuing from the speaker.
13.grammar: A noun in the genitive (the base ʿiqāb takes a final -i). The final -i here also stands in for the first-person possessive ending 'my', so the word means 'my penalty'; the possessive pronoun attaches to make the noun belong to the speaker.
13.root: ع-ق-ب (ʿ-q-b) — to follow, come after; hence requital that follows a deed

1.meaning: An interrogative formed from three pieces meaning roughly 'Is then the one who…?' It opens a rhetorical question that compares two parties. The 'a-' is a question marker, 'fa-' links to a preceding statement and means 'then/so', and 'man' is the relative pronoun 'the one who / whoever'.
1.grammar: A combination of particles plus the relative pronoun 'man'. The leading 'a-' turns the sentence into a yes/no question (often rhetorical). 'fa-' is a connective meaning 'then/so', tying the question to what came before. 'man' refers to a person and introduces a clause describing them ('the one who…'); it does not change its ending for case.

2.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
2.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

3.meaning: An active participle meaning 'standing' or 'one who stands / is upright' — also extended to mean upholding, maintaining, or being established.
3.grammar: An active participle ('standing / one standing') describing the doer of the action. The final -un ending is nominative with 'tanwīn' (indefinite, 'a …'), the case typically used for a subject or a describing predicate ('… is standing').
3.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — standing, rising, upholding

4.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
4.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

5.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
5.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

6.meaning: A noun meaning 'soul, self, person, living being.' It denotes the inner self or the whole individual — the seat of life and identity, and by extension a 'person' as a single unit.
6.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (with nunation): the genitive indefinite ('a soul'). This form appears after prepositions or in an 'of' linkage with a preceding noun (such as 'every soul').
6.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — soul, self, breath; the inner being

7.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
7.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

8.meaning: 'It earned / acquired, gained' — said of deeds and their consequences; the root means to gain or acquire something, especially the moral 'earnings' of one's actions.
8.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -t (sukūn-marked -at) suffix marks a third-person feminine singular subject, 'she/it.' The past tense presents the action as completed.
8.root: ك-س-ب (k-s-b) — to earn, acquire, gain (esp. deeds)

9.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'and they made / they set up / they appointed' — to make something into something, to render or establish it.
9.grammar: A perfect (past-tense) verb prefixed with wa- ('and'). The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (did).' (The trailing alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention.) The verb often takes two objects, in the sense 'to make X into Y.'

10.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
10.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

11.meaning: Associates, partners, or co-sharers — those set up as participants alongside another in ownership, authority, or worship. In theological usage it denotes rivals falsely placed beside Allah.
11.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of sharīk ('partner'), following the pattern faʿalāʾ. This pattern is a diptote, so it takes no nunation. The word is in the accusative case, marked by the short -a vowel on the word-final hamzah (آءَ); that hamzah is part of the plural pattern itself and cannot be split off as a separate ending. The accusative is the case typically used for the direct object of a verb ('they made/claimed partners') or after certain particles.

12.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
12.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

13.meaning: An imperative addressed to a group: 'name them!', 'designate them by name!' — a challenge to specify or identify by naming.
13.grammar: A command verb directed at a masculine plural ('you all'), shown by the -ū ending. The attached -hum ('them') is its object. So the whole is 'name them' / 'you all, name them'.
13.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, name; the act of naming or designating

14.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', specifically the 'or' that pairs with a preceding question to offer an alternative ('…or…?'). It links two possibilities being weighed against each other, often after an opening interrogative.

parts.en: or (in alternatives, esp. after a question)

14.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case or tense ending). It typically introduces the second branch of a two-part question or a balanced alternative, presenting the two as equally consequential.

15.meaning: To inform, notify, or give weighty news to someone — used of conveying significant tidings. With the endings it means 'do you (all) inform Him?'
15.grammar: A present-tense verb with the 'you all' (masculine plural) ending -ūna, which marks ongoing or factual action. The te- prefix signals second person. The attached -hu ('Him/it') is the object: 'do you (all) inform Him?'
15.root: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ) — momentous news, tidings; to announce

16.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
16.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

17.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
17.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

18.meaning: 'He/it knows' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have knowledge of, be aware of, recognize, or understand something.
18.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks 'he,' and the final -u marks the ordinary (indicative) present, 'he knows / does know.'
18.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge; knowing, being aware, recognizing

19.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
19.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

20.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
20.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

21.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', specifically the 'or' that pairs with a preceding question to offer an alternative ('…or…?'). It links two possibilities being weighed against each other, often after an opening interrogative.

parts.en: or (in alternatives, esp. after a question)

21.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case or tense ending). It typically introduces the second branch of a two-part question or a balanced alternative, presenting the two as equally consequential.

22.meaning: Something outward, apparent, or superficial — that which is merely on the surface as opposed to inner reality. The prefixed 'bi' gives 'by/with the outward (form)'.
22.grammar: An active participle ('outward thing') in the genitive after the preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -in ending (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('an outward thing') and genitive, the case required after a preposition.
22.root: ظ-ه-ر (ẓ-h-r) — to be visible, manifest, outward; the back/surface

23.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
23.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

24.meaning: Speech, an utterance, a statement, or a saying — that which is said. It denotes the act or content of speaking.
24.grammar: A definite noun ('the speech'). The -i ending is the genitive case: it typically links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of …' relationship or follows a preposition.

25.meaning: A particle of retraction meaning 'rather,' 'no, but,' or 'nay' — it cancels or sets aside what was just said and shifts to a corrected or contrasting statement that follows.
25.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it never changes form). Its function is to redirect the discourse: it dismisses a prior idea and introduces what is actually the case.

26.meaning: It was made beautiful / adorned / made alluring; the act of decorating something or making it appear attractive and appealing.
26.grammar: A past-tense verb in the passive voice on an intensive (form II) pattern, so the action is done to the subject and stresses thorough adorning ("was made beautiful/alluring"). The -u-…-i- vowel pattern marks the passive, and the final -a ending marks a third-person masculine singular subject ("it/he").

27.meaning: A compound meaning 'for those who' or 'belonging to those who'. It joins the preposition 'for/to' with a masculine plural relative pronoun ('those who'), introducing a clause that describes a group of people by something they do or possess.
27.grammar: The prefix 'li-' is a preposition meaning 'for', 'to', or expressing ownership/benefit ('belonging to'). The relative pronoun is 'alladhīna' ('those who'), but when 'li-' attaches to it the connecting hamza of 'al-' drops out and the two lām sounds merge into one doubled lām, so the form is written and read 'lilladhīna' rather than 'li-alladhīna'. 'alladhīna' has a fixed shape and does not change for case.

28.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
28.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
28.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

29.meaning: Scheming, plotting, or covert stratagem — a cunning plan, often devised in secret. With the suffix it means 'their plotting / their scheme'.
29.grammar: A noun carrying the -u (nominative) ending, the form typically used when the word is the subject of a sentence. The attached -hum ('their') makes it possessive: 'their plot'.
29.root: م-ك-ر (m-k-r) — to scheme, devise a crafty plan

30.meaning: To be turned away, barred, or hindered from something; to be diverted or obstructed. The form given is passive plural: 'they were diverted / they were barred'.
30.grammar: A past-tense passive verb (the vowel pattern ṣud-, 'they were …', not 'they …') with the masculine-plural subject ending -ū ('they'). The leading wa- means 'and'. So: 'and they were turned away / hindered'.
30.root: ص-د-د (ṣ-d-d) — to turn away, avert, obstruct

31.meaning: About / concerning; a particle marking the topic of inquiry or the thing one moves away from.
31.grammar: A preposition meaning 'about, concerning, away from'. Its base form is ʿan; the final -i here is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a connecting 'al-'. It governs the genitive case on whatever noun follows.

32.meaning: The way, road, or path — a route one travels; very often used figuratively for a course of life, conduct, or the path of religion. The attached article makes it definite: 'the way'.
32.grammar: al- is the definite article 'the' (its 'l' assimilates to the following 's', heard as 'as-sabīl'). The final -i is the genitive ending, marking the word as joined to a preceding noun ('… OF the way') or governed by a preposition.

33.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
33.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

34.meaning: He lets/leads astray — he causes someone to lose the right way, leaving them to wander from guidance.
34.grammar: A present-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he …'), in the causative pattern ('to cause to stray'). It stands in the jussive/conditional mood (the doubled lām broken apart and given a helping -i to ease pronunciation), typically meaning 'whomever he lets stray …'.
34.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray, lose the way

35.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
35.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

36.meaning: A two-part expression: 'so/then' joined to a negating word 'not.' The first piece links to what precedes (drawing a result or sequence), and the second negates the statement that follows. Together roughly: 'so… not / and so it did not…'
36.grammar: A connective particle fa- ('so, then,' showing result or sequence) plus the negating particle mā. When mā precedes a past-tense verb, it denies that the action happened ('did not…').

37.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
37.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

38.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
38.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
