39.meaning: A guide — one who shows the way, leads to the right path, or directs others toward what is correct. The indefinite form conveys 'any guide' or 'a guide (at all)'.
39.grammar: An active participle ('one who guides'). It belongs to the class of nouns ending in a weak letter, so the indefinite tanwīn shows up as -in. This -in marks it as indefinite and signals nominative/genitive case: 'a guide'.
39.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead rightly, direct

1.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
1.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

2.meaning: Painful punishment, torment, or chastisement — suffering imposed as a penalty.
2.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject or for the thing said to exist.

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
3.root: — (particle)

4.meaning: 'The life' — living existence, the state of being alive.
4.grammar: The definite article al- with the feminine noun ḥayāt ('life'); the waw belongs to the stem and the tā' marbūṭa is its feminine suffix. The final -i is the genitive case vowel, which typically marks the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a following noun.

5.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
5.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
5.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

6.meaning: Severe suffering, torment, or punishment inflicted as chastisement. The prefixes add emphasis and definiteness: 'and surely the punishment …'.
6.grammar: A noun with the -u (nominative) ending, the case used for a sentence's subject. The la- prefix is an emphatic 'surely/indeed', and wa- is 'and'. Together: 'and surely the punishment …'.
6.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to torment, punish, cause pain

7.meaning: The Hereafter — the final, lasting life that comes after death and the present world; literally 'the last/latter (abode or life)', as opposed to the first, nearer life.
7.grammar: A feminine adjective used as a noun, with 'the'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …'), or follows a preposition or oath particle.
7.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after, end

8.meaning: More severe, harder, or more grievous — a comparative describing something that is more difficult or distressing than another.
8.grammar: A comparative/superlative adjective on the pattern 'aCCaC ('more …'). The -u ending marks the nominative case, typical for a predicate or subject. It conveys 'harder / more severe'.
8.root: ش-ق-ق (sh-q-q) — hardship, difficulty, splitting; to be arduous

9.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
9.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

10.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
10.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

11.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
11.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

12.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
12.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

13.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
13.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

14.meaning: A protector, shielder, or defender — one who guards and wards off harm. The indefinite form means 'any protector' or 'a defender (at all)'.
14.grammar: An active participle ('one who protects') from the class of nouns ending in a weak letter, so its indefinite tanwīn appears as -in, marking it indefinite and nominative/genitive. The wa- prefix means 'and': 'and a protector'.
14.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, shield, protect from harm

1.meaning: A likeness, comparison, parable, or illustrative example; a similitude used to make something abstract vivid and understandable.
1.grammar: A singular noun with the -u (nominative) ending, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being described. Being without tanwīn here, it commonly stands as the first term of a possessive phrase ('the likeness OF …').
1.root: م-ث-ل (m-th-l) — to resemble; likeness, similitude, example

2.meaning: The Garden / Paradise — a definite noun literally meaning 'the garden'; the term for the Garden of Paradise, the abode of reward in the Hereafter.
2.grammar: Definite noun: 'al-' is 'the'. The '-i' ending (on the feminine '-at-') is genitive, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …') or follows a preposition. 'janna' originally means a lush, shaded garden.
2.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal (a garden's dense foliage 'covers' the ground)

3.meaning: A feminine singular relative pronoun: 'the one which / that which / who' (referring to a single feminine thing). It introduces a descriptive clause that tells us more about a preceding feminine noun.
3.grammar: A relative pronoun, feminine singular, fixed in form (it does not change for case). It links a feminine noun to a following clause describing it, the equivalent of English 'which,' 'that,' or 'who.'

4.meaning: To be promised — to have a pledge or assurance made about something, whether of reward or of threatened consequence. The form is passive: 'it was/has been promised'.
4.grammar: A past-tense passive verb (vowel pattern wuʿi-, 'was promised') in the third-person masculine singular, shown by the final -a ('he/it'). So: 'he/it was promised'.
4.root: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — to promise, pledge, give assurance

5.meaning: Those who have taqwā — the God-conscious, the mindful and dutiful. It describes people who keep a vigilant awareness of Allah, guarding themselves against wrongdoing and shielding themselves from His displeasure out of reverent care.

parts.en: one who is God-conscious / guards himself

5.grammar: The l- prefix is 'the'. This is an active participle (one who does the action). The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the subject (nominative) form, i.e. the ones who carry out the guarding/mindfulness.
5.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, protect, shield oneself

6.meaning: A verb 'it flows, runs, streams' — used of water and rivers moving along, and of things that run or course freely. It describes continuous, ongoing motion.
6.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd person feminine singular. The ta- prefix here marks a feminine 'it/she' subject. The verb describes an ongoing or habitual action: 'it flows / keeps flowing.'
6.root: ج-ر-ي (j-r-y) — to flow, run, stream

7.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
7.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

8.meaning: 'Beneath it / underneath it' — the noun for the underside or lower region of something, with an attached pronoun 'its' (referring to a feminine thing). It points to the space below or underneath a thing.
8.grammar: A location noun ('underneath') with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('its/her'), referring to a feminine noun. The -i ending is the genitive case, normally triggered here because words of place like 'under' commonly follow a preposition such as 'from' (min taḥti = 'from beneath').
8.root: ت-ح-ت (t-ḥ-t) — underneath, below

9.meaning: 'The rivers / the streams' — the definite plural of a word for a flowing river or watercourse. It denotes large, running channels of water.
9.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the rivers'). The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence — the doer of the verb or the thing being described.

10.meaning: Food, produce, or that which is eaten — the edible yield (as of a tree or land). With the suffix it means 'its food / its produce'.
10.grammar: A noun with the -u (nominative) ending, the form used for a sentence's subject. The attached -hā ('its/her') makes it possessive: 'its food / its produce'.
10.root: أ-ك-ل (ʾ-k-l) — to eat; food, that which is eaten

11.meaning: Lasting, perpetual, continuous, or everlasting — something that endures without ceasing.
11.grammar: An active participle ('one that lasts') used adjectivally. The -un ending (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative case, the case typical of a subject or predicate: 'lasting / everlasting'.

12.meaning: Shade or shadow — the cool, sheltering shade cast by something. With the suffix it means 'its shade'.
12.grammar: A noun with the -u (nominative) ending, used for a subject. The leading wa- is 'and', and the attached -hā ('its/her') is possessive: 'and its shade'.
12.root: ظ-ل-ل (ẓ-l-l) — shade, shadow, shelter; to remain/overshadow

13.meaning: That; a demonstrative used to point to something distant or already mentioned. It singles out a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing, roughly 'that one over there.'
13.grammar: A feminine singular demonstrative pronoun pointing to something far off. The -ka element signals remoteness ('that yonder' rather than 'this near'). Being a demonstrative, it does not take case endings; its form is fixed.

14.meaning: The outcome, final result, or end-consequence of a matter; what ultimately comes after and follows from something — its sequel or final reward.
14.grammar: A feminine singular noun on the 'fuʿlā' pattern, denoting the end-result or aftermath of a course of action. Its final long 'ā' is fixed and does not change for the usual case-endings; as the first term of a possessive construction it conveys 'the outcome of …'.
14.root: ع-ق-ب (ʿ-q-b) — following after, succession, consequence, end-result

15.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
15.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

16.meaning: To guard oneself against harm, to be mindful and wary of wrongdoing, to hold oneself back in reverent caution — the act of God-conscious self-protection. The form is past plural: 'they guarded themselves / were mindful'.
16.grammar: A past-tense verb of the 'iftaʿala' pattern, here with the masculine-plural ending -aw ('they'). It denotes a completed action by a group: 'they guarded themselves / were God-conscious'.
16.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, shield, protect; reverent self-protection

17.meaning: The final outcome, the end-result, or the ultimate sequel of a matter — what one ends up with after all is over. With the suffix it conveys 'and the final end of …'.
17.grammar: A noun ending in the fixed long vowel -ā (a non-inflecting feminine pattern), so its ending does not change for case. The leading wa- means 'and': 'and the final outcome'.
17.root: ع-ق-ب (ʿ-q-b) — to follow, come after; the end that follows

18.meaning: The disbelievers / the ungrateful — those who reject faith and cover over the truth; the word also carries the sense of covering up or being ungrateful for what one has been given.
18.grammar: 'al-' is 'the'. The stem is an active participle ('one who disbelieves/is ungrateful') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the accusative/genitive form of the sound masculine plural: it marks the word as an object of a verb or as governed by a preposition, as opposed to the subject form -ūna.
18.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; ingratitude, disbelief

19.meaning: The Fire — a definite noun for fire; frequently the term for the blazing punishment of the Hereafter (Hell).
19.grammar: Definite noun: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the following 'n', heard as 'an-nār'). The '-u' ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject of a sentence or the doer of an action.

1.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

2.meaning: We gave them / We granted them — a completed act of bestowing or conferring something upon a group, done by 'We'.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb of Form IV ('to give, bestow, grant'). The suffix -nā marks the doer as 'we'. The attached pronoun -hum(u) is the object, 'them' (a group); its vowel is lengthened to -humu to ease pronunciation before the next word. Altogether: 'We gave them'.
2.root: ء-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (Form IV) to give, bring, bestow

3.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
3.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
3.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

4.meaning: 'They rejoice / are glad.' The verb means to feel joy, delight, or elation — sometimes wholesome gladness, sometimes exultant self-satisfaction depending on context.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb. The -ūna ending marks a plural masculine subject ('they') and signals the ordinary (indicative) present tense — an action ongoing or habitual.
4.root: ف-ر-ح (f-r-ḥ) — to rejoice, be glad, exult

5.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
5.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

6.meaning: 'It was sent down / revealed': the act of being caused to descend, used especially of revelation brought down from Allah. The passive form puts the focus on the thing sent down rather than on the sender.
6.grammar: A past-tense passive verb in Form IV (anzala 'to send down' → unzila 'was sent down'). The prefix is only the u- vowel carried on the connecting hamza; the nūn that follows is the first root letter (of ن-ز-ل), not part of the prefix. The internal vowel pattern u–i marks it as passive ('was/were sent down'), with no named doer. The final -a marks the subject as 'he/it', a single masculine thing, and signals completed action.
6.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down; (Form IV) to send down

7.meaning: 'To you' (addressing one person): indicating direction or motion toward a single individual — that toward which something moves or is directed.
7.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, towards') with an attached pronoun; before a suffix ilā takes the form ilay-. The -ka ending is the pronoun 'you' for a single male addressee. Pronouns following a preposition stand in the genitive relationship, though their form does not visibly change for case.

8.meaning: A connector meaning 'and', joined to the preposition 'from / of', introducing a portion or origin — 'and from' or 'and among'.
8.grammar: Two particles: wa- ('and') plus the preposition min ('from, of, among'). Min normally appears as 'min', but its final vowel shifts to 'mina' when the next word begins with the definite article, simply to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.
8.root: — (particles)

9.meaning: The factions / confederates / parties — groups banded together, especially allied bands or hostile coalitions. 'aḥzāb' is the plural of 'ḥizb', a party or group.
9.grammar: A definite broken (irregular) plural noun, 'the factions/parties'. The '-i' ending is genitive, the case a noun takes after a preposition or as the second term of an 'of' linkage ('... of the factions'). 'al-' means 'the'.

10.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
10.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

11.meaning: To deny, reject, refuse to acknowledge, or disapprove of something. The form is present-tense third person: 'he denies / one denies'.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular: the ye- prefix means 'he/it', and the final -u marks the ordinary (indicative) present, signalling an ongoing or habitual action: 'he denies / rejects'.
11.root: ن-ك-ر (n-k-r) — to not recognize, deny, disavow, reject

12.meaning: Part of it / some of it. Baʿḍ denotes a portion or some members of a larger whole, here joined to a possessive 'it.'
12.grammar: A noun meaning 'a part / some.' The -a ending is accusative, the case typically used for a direct object. The attached -hu ('its/his') is a possessive pronoun, giving 'part of it.'

13.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
13.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

14.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
14.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

15.meaning: 'I was commanded', 'I have been ordered / instructed'. It expresses that the speaker is the recipient of a command — someone else has issued an order and the speaker is bound by it.

parts.en: passive vowel: the action was done to the subject

15.grammar: Past-tense passive verb. The -tu ending means the subject is 'I', and the opening u-vowel makes it passive ('I was commanded' rather than 'I commanded'). The action is presented as completed.

16.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
16.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

17.meaning: 'That I worship / serve' — to worship, to serve in humble devotion and obedience as a servant before his Master.
17.grammar: A present-tense verb. The a- prefix marks a first-person singular subject ('I'). The final -a is the subjunctive ending, taken when the verb is governed by a preceding particle (such as 'that/to'), giving the sense 'that I worship' or 'to worship'.

18.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
18.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

19.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
19.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

20.meaning: To make something a partner or associate alongside another — especially to set up partners beside Allah. The form is passive first-person: '(that) I be made to associate' or 'partners be associated by me'.
20.grammar: A present-tense passive verb of the 'afʿala' pattern. The final -a is the subjunctive mood, the form used after 'that / to' to express purpose or what is intended: '(that) partners be associated'. The u- prefix signals the passive ('be made to associate').
20.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, partner; associating partners (with Allah)

21.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
21.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

22.meaning: 'To Him' or 'toward Him' — the preposition expressing direction or endpoint ('to / toward') combined with a pronoun referring to a single masculine person, indicating motion or attention directed at him.
22.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base 'ilā shifts to 'ilay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -hi is the third-person masculine singular object of a preposition, 'him'; its -i vowel is the form the pronoun takes after the 'ay' sound.

23.meaning: Means "I call, I invite, I summon" — the act of calling out to or inviting someone (often calling people toward something), ongoing and done by "I."
23.grammar: A present/ongoing verb. The a- prefix marks "I" as the doer. The verb ends in the long vowel -ū of the weak-final root (the written alif after it is a silent spelling convention). Its sense is to call upon, invite, or summon.
23.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, invite, summon, supplicate

24.meaning: And to Him / toward Him. The wa- means 'and'; ilā is the preposition 'to/toward' indicating direction or destination; the attached pronoun -hi means 'him'.
24.grammar: Wa- means 'and'. Ilā ('to/toward') is a preposition of direction; it takes the special form 'ilay-' before a pronoun. The attached -hi is the genitive pronoun 'him', the form pronouns take after prepositions; the -i vowel reflects that genitive attachment.

25.meaning: A place or point of return, a destination to which one comes back, a final resort. With the attached 'my', it means 'my return / my place of returning'.
25.grammar: A noun of place ('place to which one returns') in the genitive (base maʾāb takes -i). The final -i also serves as the first-person possessive 'my', so the word means 'my place of return'.
25.root: أ-و-ب (ʾ-w-b) — to return, come back, turn back

1.meaning: 'And likewise / and in the same way / and thus' — a connective phrase pointing back to a manner just mentioned and saying 'in that very way…'. Built from 'and' + 'like' + 'that'.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'; the prefix ka- means 'like/as'; 'dhālika' is the demonstrative 'that' (pointing to something distant or already mentioned). Because ka- acts like a preposition, the word after it stands in the genitive, though the demonstrative 'dhālika' keeps a fixed form and shows no visible case change. The whole means 'and just like that / and thus'.

2.meaning: 'We sent it down / revealed it'. Past-tense verb from anzala ('to send down, cause to descend'), with the 'We' of majesty as subject and 'it' as object. Characteristically used of revelation sent down from above.

parts.en: sent down / caused to descend (causative stem)

2.grammar: A past-tense verb of the causative pattern (af ʿala: 'to make come down'). The suffix -nā marks a first-person plural subject, 'we'. The attached -hu is the object 'it/him'. In divine speech the plural 'We' conveys majesty, not number.
2.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to come down, descend; (causative) to send down

3.meaning: Judgement or sound ruling, considered as a quality or capacity — the ability to decide rightly and govern with wisdom. The indefinite form points to 'judgement' in general rather than one particular verdict.
3.grammar: A noun in the accusative state with tanwīn (the -an ending), which marks it as indefinite ('a judgement') and as the object of a verb or a specifying complement (telling in what respect something is so).
3.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, decide, govern with wisdom

4.meaning: An adjective meaning 'Arabic' — pertaining to the Arabs or to their language; that which is in clear, eloquent Arabic speech.
4.grammar: A relational adjective formed with the -iyy suffix ('belonging to / characterized by'). The final -an (tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative: it marks an indefinite descriptive word agreeing with an indefinite accusative noun it qualifies ('an Arabic …').

5.meaning: And surely if — a combination meaning 'and if', strengthened by an emphatic particle so it reads 'and indeed, should it be that …'.
5.grammar: A cluster of particles: wa- ('and'), an emphatic la- ('surely, indeed') that strengthens what follows, and in ('if') introducing a condition. The final short -i is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before the next word. Together they set up an emphatic conditional, 'and surely if …'.

6.meaning: You followed / you took as a guide — completed action of going after and adhering to someone's way.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb of Form VIII (reflexive 'to follow after, take as a guide'); the initial helping 'i' and doubled 'tt' belong to this pattern. The suffix -ta marks the doer as second-person masculine singular ('you', one male). It states a completed act of following.
6.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, pursue

7.meaning: Their desires, inclinations, cravings; the pulls of personal whim and passion — what one leans toward apart from guidance, here belonging to 'them'.
7.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of hawā ('desire, inclination, whim'). The case-vowel -a (accusative) typically marks the object of a verb. The attached pronoun -hum means 'their' (a group of males or mixed). Altogether: 'their desires/whims'.
7.root: ه-و-ي (h-w-y) — inclination, desire, whim; to incline toward, to fall

8.meaning: "After what…" — a time expression "baʿda" (after) joined to "mā" (what/that which), together meaning "after the fact that" or "following what (happened)."
8.grammar: An adverb of time, "baʿda" (after), which is always followed by a noun or clause; its fixed '-a' ending reflects its governing (genitive-attaching) role. "Mā" is a connective "what / the fact that," introducing the clause that follows.
8.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — to be after, distant; afterness

9.meaning: It came to you / reached you — a completed arrival of something reaching a person (one male).
9.grammar: A past-tense verb, 'he/it came', whose final -a vowel is the inherent third-person masculine singular inflection built into the verb form itself (not a separate piece). The attached pronoun -ka ('you', one male) is the object reached — 'it came to you'.

10.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
10.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

11.meaning: The knowledge; sure and certain knowing, established information and understanding (with the definite article).
11.grammar: A definite verbal noun: al- means 'the'. The final -i is the genitive ending, which typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship. It denotes knowledge as a settled, certain thing.

12.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
12.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

13.meaning: 'For You / to You' — a 'for/to' particle attached to the pronoun 'You,' indicating that something is directed toward, or done for the sake of, a single addressee.
13.grammar: A small phrase: the particle li- ('for / to,' vowelled la- before a pronoun) joined to the attached pronoun -ka, 'you' (one masculine addressee). The pronoun is in the form used as the object of a preposition, marking the person as the one to whom or for whom the action is directed.

14.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
14.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

15.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
15.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

16.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
16.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

17.meaning: Guardian, protector, ally, patron — one who is close to another and takes charge of their care, support, and protection; a trusted friend who stands by and acts on one's behalf.
17.grammar: A noun on the intensive faʿīl pattern, here preceded by the joining word wa- ('and'). The final -in is the indefinite genitive (nunation): no 'the', and the genitive case — the form a noun takes after a preposition such as min ('from').
17.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to be near, to be in charge of; closeness, guardianship, alliance

18.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
18.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

19.meaning: A protector, shielder, or defender — one who guards and wards off harm. The indefinite form means 'any protector' or 'a defender (at all)'.
19.grammar: An active participle ('one who protects') from the class of nouns ending in a weak letter, so its indefinite tanwīn shows up as -in, marking it indefinite and nominative/genitive: 'a protector / defender'.
19.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, shield, protect from harm

1.meaning: "And indeed / and most certainly" — combines 'and' with the emphatic 'la-' and the particle 'qad'; before a past-tense verb 'qad' affirms that the action has definitely and already happened, reinforced into 'and indeed it surely did'.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'and' plus the emphatic 'la-' ('surely') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' stresses that the act is real and completed ('has indeed happened'); together they form a strong oath-like affirmation. These are function words and are not inflected.

2.meaning: We sent / dispatched. From the causative verb meaning to send forth or commission, especially the sending of messengers; with 'We' as the subject.
2.grammar: Past/perfect verb in the causative (form IV) pattern meaning 'to send', 1st person plural ('we'). The suffix -nā is the subject ending 'we' on a completed action. The perfect tense presents the sending as accomplished and complete.

3.meaning: 'messengers' — envoys, those sent by Allah bearing a message to people.
3.grammar: The broken (irregular) plural of rasūl ('messenger'). The -an ending is accusative with tanwīn, typically marking the word as a direct object and indefinite ('messengers').
3.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; messenger, message

4.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
4.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

5.meaning: 'Before you' (in time or place): the period or position prior to a single person — that which comes earlier or stands in front, relative to one addressee.
5.grammar: The adverb/noun qabl ('before, prior') with the attached pronoun -ka ('you', a single male). The -i ending on qabl is genitive, the case regularly taken after a preposition (such as min, 'from before') and when a noun is linked to a following possessor; here it is linked to the pronoun 'you' ('before-you').
5.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, be before; priority, what comes first

6.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'We made / appointed / rendered.' This very common verb can mean to create or place something, or to assign something a state or role (to make X into Y).
6.grammar: A completed (past-tense) action. The -nā ending marks 'we' as the doers. The verb often takes two objects, meaning 'to make/turn one thing into another.'
6.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, place, render, appoint

7.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
7.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

8.meaning: A noun meaning 'spouses', 'mates', or 'wives' — the plural of a word denoting one of a pair joined together, hence a husband or wife. Context determines whether husbands or wives are meant.
8.grammar: A plural noun with the -an ending, which is accusative and indefinite. The accusative typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon). The azC-ā-C shape is a broken-plural pattern. The singular denotes either partner of a married pair.
8.root: ز-و-ج (z-w-j) — to pair, to join as a couple; spouse, mate

9.meaning: Offspring, progeny, descendants — one's children and seed, the line that issues from a person. The indefinite ending conveys 'offspring' as an indefinite group.
9.grammar: A noun with the -an (tanwīn) ending, which marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case — the case typically used for the object of a verb or an item being listed. The wa- prefix means 'and': 'and offspring'.
9.root: ذ-ر-ر (dh-r-r) — to scatter, multiply; progeny, descendants

10.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
10.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

11.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

11.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

12.meaning: To or for a messenger — someone sent with a commission; a person dispatched to convey a message on behalf of the one who sent him. In the religious sense, a prophet entrusted to deliver revelation.
12.grammar: A noun preceded by the preposition 'li' (to/for). The final '-in' (tanwīn kasra) is the indefinite genitive: it marks the word as 'a messenger' (no 'the') and is the case required after the preposition.
12.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send, dispatch a message

13.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
13.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

14.meaning: '(that) it comes' or 'so that it may come' — to arrive, come, or approach. The verb denotes something drawing near or coming to pass.
14.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The final -a (subjunctive) ending, rather than the usual -u, signals that the verb is governed by a preceding particle such as 'that' or 'before/until' — giving the sense 'that it come' or 'so that it may come.'

15.meaning: With a sign — by means of an indicative token, miracle, or evidentiary proof that points to a truth.
15.grammar: The prefix bi- means 'with / by means of' and always pulls the following noun into the genitive. The final -in (tanwīn) is the indefinite genitive: 'with a sign', the ending required after this preposition and marking the noun as indefinite ('a', not 'the').
15.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — sign, mark, token; a verse of scripture

16.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
16.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

17.meaning: 'By the leave of / with the permission of' — formed from 'with/by' plus 'permission, leave, sanction'. It conveys that something happens by someone's authorization or enabling will.
17.grammar: The prefix bi- is a preposition 'with/by'. The noun 'idhn' means 'permission, leave, sanction'. After the preposition it takes the genitive -i ending, the form used following a preposition and typically linking on to a following noun ('the permission OF …').
17.root: أ-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — to permit, give leave; also listening/ear

18.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
18.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

19.meaning: For each, for every — combines the preposition 'for/to' with 'each/every (one)'. Kull expresses totality taken one by one.
19.grammar: The noun kull ('each/every/all') preceded by the preposition li- ('for'). The -i ending is genitive, the case regularly required after a preposition, and which also lets kull link to a following noun ('each OF …').

20.meaning: A noun meaning 'a fixed term, an appointed time, a set deadline, a span allotted before something falls due.' It denotes the limit or end-point of a period.
20.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (with nunation): the genitive indefinite ('a term'). This form occurs after a preposition or in an 'of' linkage with a preceding noun.
20.root: ا-ج-ل (ʾ-j-l) — appointed term, fixed time, deadline

21.meaning: A writing, a written record, or a prescribed decree — that which is written down and thereby ordained or fixed. The indefinite form means 'a writing / a decree'.
21.grammar: A noun with the -un (tanwīn) ending, marking it as indefinite and in the nominative case — the case used for a subject or predicate: 'a writing / a prescribed decree'.
21.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; that which is written, decreed, prescribed

1.meaning: To wipe out, erase, efface, or blot out — to remove something so it leaves no trace. The form is present-tense third person: 'he/it erases'.
1.grammar: A present-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular. The ye- prefix means 'he/it'; the verb ends in a long -ū because its final root letter is weak, where a plain present tense would otherwise show a short -u. It signals ongoing action: 'he/it erases / blots out'.
1.root: م-ح-و (m-ḥ-w) — to wipe out, efface, erase

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
2.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

3.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
3.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

4.meaning: "He wills / wishes / desires" — denotes an act of will or volition, the choosing of something. As an ongoing/present-tense verb it expresses willing as a continuous, sovereign act.
4.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in the 'he' form. The ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular ('he'). The final -u ending is the indicative mood, marking a plain, ongoing statement of fact ('he wills').

5.meaning: To make firm, establish, confirm, or fix in place — to leave standing and affirmed (the opposite of erasing). The form is present-tense third person: 'he/it confirms / establishes'.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb of the 'afʿala' (causative) pattern, third-person masculine singular: the ye- prefix means 'he/it', and the final -u marks the ordinary (indicative) present of ongoing action. The wa- prefix is 'and': 'and he/it confirms / establishes'.
5.root: ث-ب-ت (th-b-t) — to be firm, fixed, steadfast; to establish

6.meaning: 'And with Him / in His possession' — 'ʿinda' means at, with, in the presence or keeping of someone, often implying ownership or that something rests in their hands; with the attached 'Him' it means 'with Him / in His possession'.

parts.en: with / in the presence or keeping of

6.grammar: An adverb of place/possession ('ʿinda', 'with/at') fixed in the accusative '-a' form, joined to the attached pronoun '-hu' ('him/his'). Together they express that something is in His presence or possession. Prefixed 'wa' means 'and'.
6.root: — (preposition/adverb; no triliteral root)

7.meaning: Mother; and by extension the source, origin, or foundation from which other things derive. Conveys the idea of an original, governing basis to which the rest is referred.
7.grammar: A noun whose final -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate identifying who/what something is. Without nunation, it reads as definite or as the first term of a possessive ('mother/foundation OF …'), being joined to a following noun.
7.root: أ-م-م (ʾ-m-m) — to head toward; source, origin, mother

8.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
8.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.
8.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — writing, inscribing, recording

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
1.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

2.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
2.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

3.meaning: 'We will surely show you' — to cause someone to see something, to let them witness it, here stressed as a certain, emphatic promise.
3.grammar: Present-tense causative (form IV) verb, 'to make [someone] see / to show.' The nu- prefix marks a first-person plural subject ('we'), the attached -ka is the object 'you' (one male), and the heavy -nna fused before it is the emphatic ending that turns the verb into a solemn assurance ('We shall most certainly show you').
3.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — seeing, perceiving

4.meaning: a part of / some of / a portion of — a noun denoting a piece or fraction of a larger whole (in the accusative form).
4.grammar: A noun meaning 'part' or 'some'. The final -a ending is accusative, marking it as a direct object or, with a measure of time, an adverbial span. It is normally followed by a noun in the genitive ('part of …').
4.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, a portion, some

5.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
5.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

6.meaning: To promise something to someone — to pledge or give an assurance that a thing (whether reward or threat) will come about.
6.grammar: Present-tense verb with a first-person plural subject marked by the na- prefix ('we'). The attached -hum is the object 'them' (a male/mixed group). The stem's indicative -u ending (just before the object) marks a plain ongoing or general action ('we promise them').
6.root: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — promising, pledging

7.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
7.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

8.meaning: 'We will surely take you fully (in death)' — to take a soul completely, to receive someone in full at the end of life; emphatically stated as a sure outcome.

parts.en: take fully / cause to pass away (intensive stem)

8.grammar: Present-tense verb of the intensive (form V) pattern conveying taking something in full — commonly the taking of a soul at death. The na- prefix marks a first-person plural subject ('we'), the attached -ka is the object 'you' (one male), and the heavy -nna fused before it is the emphatic ending making it a solemn certainty ('We shall most surely take you').
8.root: و-ف-ي (w-f-y) — fullness, completing, paying in full

9.meaning: A compound particle 'so it is only …' or 'then indeed only.' It joins a consequence ('so/then') to an emphatic restriction ('only / nothing more than'), confining the statement to exactly what follows.
9.grammar: A cluster of particles: 'fa-' introduces a result ('so/then'), 'inna' gives emphasis ('truly'), and the attached 'mā' turns the emphasis into restriction, so the whole means 'so it is only/nothing but.' These are connective and emphatic words; they have no case ending of their own.

10.meaning: "upon you / to you / against you" — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over') with the 'you' pronoun, carrying senses of resting upon, being directed to, or bearing upon someone.
10.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base ʿalā shifts to ʿalay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -ka means 'you' (second-person masculine singular). Prepositions themselves take no case ending.

11.meaning: The conveying / the delivering (of a message): the act of passing on and communicating something so it reaches its hearers fully and clearly; a verbal noun naming that act.
11.grammar: A definite verbal noun (a noun naming an action) with the prefixed article 'al-' ('the'). The final -u is the nominative case ending, typically marking the word as the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified ('… is …').
11.root: ب-ل-غ (b-l-gh) — to reach, to arrive at; to convey

12.meaning: "and upon Us" — the conjunction "and" joined to a preposition meaning "on/upon," carrying the sense of an obligation or responsibility that rests upon the speakers. When fronted, this phrase conveys that the matter falls to the speakers as their charge.
12.grammar: Built from the conjunction wa- ("and") plus the preposition ʿalā ("upon"), whose form shifts to ʿalay- before an attached pronoun. The suffix -nā is the attached object pronoun "us." A preposition with this pronoun typically conveys that something lies upon or is owed by "us."

13.meaning: the reckoning, accounting, or calling-to-account — the act of tallying up deeds and settling what is due, as a debtor's account is audited and balanced.
13.grammar: A definite noun: the prefix al- means "the." The final -u is the nominative ending, which generally marks the word as the subject of a verb or the thing being identified ("the reckoning is …").

1.meaning: A compound opening a question and a negation at once: roughly 'and have … not …?' or 'is it not the case that …?'. It combines a questioning particle, the connector 'and', and a negative that places the following verb in the past, often expecting the listener to agree.
1.grammar: Three particles fused together: the interrogative 'a-' (turning the statement into a question), the connector 'wa' ('and'), and the negator 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and shifts its meaning into the past ('has not / did not'), and it puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (vowel-less) form. The combination often invites the listener to affirm ('have you not …?').

2.meaning: To see, perceive, or behold — and, by extension, to realize, observe, or come to recognize. The bare form here is the 'cut-short' (jussive) shape used after certain particles, so it reads 'they (do not) see'.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb in its shortened (jussive) form, used after particles such as those that negate the past or express purpose/condition. The third-person masculine plural subject 'they' here takes the distinct jussive plural ending '-aw' (written wāw + a silent 'alif al-fāriqa). This '-aw' is the jussive paradigm's own ending in its own right, not the indicative '-ūna' with the 'na' stripped off.

3.meaning: That We … — an emphatic linking particle 'that' fused with the pronoun 'We.' 'Anna' introduces and asserts a fact ('that indeed …'), and the attached 'We' names the doer (a majestic or plural 'We').
3.grammar: An emphatic particle 'anna' ('that, indeed') with the attached pronoun -nā 'we.' This family of particles takes a following noun/pronoun in the accusative as its subject, so -nā here functions as that subject: 'that We …'. It firmly introduces a stated fact.

4.meaning: "we come / we bring," or "we approach" — to advance toward something or to bring something about, expressed by the speakers as an ongoing or habitual action.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb. The na- prefix marks the subject as "we," and the present form signals an action that is ongoing, repeated, or yet to be completed. Derived from the verb atā ("to come, to bring").

5.meaning: 'the earth,' 'the ground,' 'the land' — the earth as a whole, or the land/ground beneath us. It denotes the terrestrial expanse on which creatures live and walk.
5.grammar: A definite noun ('the earth'). The '-a' ending marks the accusative (the 'object' case) — the role of the thing acted upon, e.g. the direct object of a verb. The prefixed 'al-' makes it definite, 'the earth.'

6.meaning: "we diminish it / we reduce it" — the speakers' act of decreasing, cutting down, or making something less, with "it" referring to a feminine thing being reduced.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb with the na- prefix marking "we" as the subject and the present form indicating ongoing or repeated action. The ending -u is the indicative present marker. The attached -hā is the object pronoun "it" for a grammatically feminine thing.
6.root: ن-ق-ص (n-q-ṣ) — to decrease, diminish, fall short

7.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
7.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

8.meaning: "its outlying parts / its edges, borders, extremities" — the outermost regions or sides of something, here belonging to a feminine entity.
8.grammar: A plural noun ("edges, extremities," plural of ṭaraf) with the attached possessive pronoun -hā ("its," feminine). The -i ending is genitive, which typically marks possession or follows a preposition; with a following pronoun it signals "the edges OF it."
8.root: ط-ر-ف (ṭ-r-f) — extremity, edge, outermost part

9.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
9.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
9.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

10.meaning: He judges / He will judge; He decides, rules, and decrees with authority — passing a binding verdict and governing a matter wisely.
10.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, 'he judges/will judge,' describing a single male subject (or 'He,' of Allah). The ya- prefix marks the third-person masculine singular ('he'), and the final -u marks the indicative mood — an actual, ongoing, or future action.
10.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, decide, rule; wisdom and governance

11.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
11.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

12.meaning: one who reverses, overturns, or follows up to revoke — an agent who comes after a decision to push it back, repeal it, or call it into review. Often used in the sense of someone able to overturn or amend a verdict.
12.grammar: An active participle (a "doer" noun) formed with the mu- prefix, naming the one who performs the action. The -a ending is accusative, which generally marks a word as the object of a verb or as the noun governed by a negating particle ("there is no ___").
12.root: ع-ق-ب (ʿ-q-b) — to follow, come after; heel, consequence

13.meaning: "to / for His decree" — a preposition meaning "for, to" joined to a noun meaning "judgment, ruling, command, or decree," with "His" referring to a single male possessor.
13.grammar: The prefix li- is a preposition ("to, for"). The noun ḥukm ("judgment, ruling, decree") takes the genitive -i ending, which is required after a preposition. The attached -hi is the possessive pronoun "his," appearing as -hi (rather than -hu) when it follows an -i sound.
13.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, rule, decree; wisdom

14.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
14.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

15.meaning: Swift, quick, fast — describing one who is rapid in carrying out something. Used of Allah, it conveys that an action (such as reckoning) is accomplished with utter speed.
15.grammar: An adjective in the intensive 'faʿīl' pattern (denoting a strong, inherent quality). The final -u (ḍamma) marks the nominative case; with no tanwīn here it is in a possessive construction, 'swift of …,' linking it to a following noun.

16.meaning: The reckoning, accounting, or calling to account — the tallying and settling of deeds; also calculation or counting in a general sense.
16.grammar: A definite verbal noun with the article 'al-' ('the'). The final -i (kasra) marks the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or as the second part of a possessive pair ('… of the reckoning').

1.meaning: 'And indeed / while already' — the word 'wa' ('and, while') joined to 'qad', a particle that, before a past-tense verb, stresses that the action has certainly and already happened.
1.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and', or circumstantial 'while') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' emphasizes completion and certainty ('has indeed already…'); with a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes' or 'may'.

2.meaning: "he plotted / he schemed," or more neutrally "he devised a stratagem" — to plan covertly, often by way of cunning or deception to outmaneuver another.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb. The bare three-letter form with the final -a marks the subject as "he" and reports a single completed action in the past. Derived from makara ("to plot, scheme").
2.root: م-ك-ر (m-k-r) — to plot, scheme, devise a stratagem

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
4.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

5.meaning: 'Before them' in time — denoting what came earlier, the period or persons preceding a masculine plural group.
5.grammar: An adverb of time, 'before,' carrying the genitive ending -i because it is linked to a following possessor. The attached 'him' means 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group), giving 'before them.' The -i ending reflects that the word is governed in a possessive link.
5.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, come before; before/prior

6.meaning: Then belonging to Allah; so it is Allah's. The phrase asserts that something pertains or belongs exclusively to Allah, introduced by a connective 'then/so'.
6.grammar: A connective 'fa-' ('then/so') plus the preposition 'li-' ('to/for/belonging to') attached to the name Allah. The '-i' ending on the name is genitive, the case required after a preposition; the combination expresses ownership or entitlement: '(it is) for/belonging to Allah'.
6.root: — (the proper name Allah)

7.meaning: the scheming, the plotting, the stratagem — a planned device or ruse worked out in secret to gain an advantage.
7.grammar: A definite noun: the prefix al- means "the." The final -u is the nominative ending, which generally marks the word as the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified.
7.root: م-ك-ر (m-k-r) — to plot, scheme, devise a stratagem

8.meaning: A word meaning 'all together', 'all of them', or 'the whole lot' — emphasising that no one and nothing is left out of a group.
8.grammar: A noun meaning 'all/entirety' carrying the -an ending: accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite '-n'). This accusative form is typical of a word that comes alongside another to specify it as 'all of them, every one', describing the manner or extent.
8.root: ج-م-ع (j-m-ʿ) — gathering, joining, bringing together

9.meaning: 'He/it knows' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have knowledge of, be aware of, recognize, or understand something.
9.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks 'he,' and the final -u marks the ordinary (indicative) present, 'he knows / does know.'
9.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge; knowing, being aware, recognizing

10.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
10.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

11.meaning: He/it earns, acquires, gains — to gather to oneself, especially the consequences of one's own deeds, whether good or bad. The verb stresses what a person brings upon themselves by their actions.
11.grammar: A present/imperfect verb. The ta- prefix marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('she/it …') or a second-person masculine singular ('you …'); context decides which. The final -u is the indicative ('plain present') ending, signalling ongoing or habitual action: 'earns / is earning'.

12.meaning: A noun meaning 'all, every, each, the whole of.' It expresses totality — when joined to a following noun it means 'every (one)' or 'the entirety of' that thing.
12.grammar: A noun of totality with the final -u ending (nominative). The -u typically marks it as the subject or the thing being spoken about. It normally attaches to a following noun to mean 'every / all of' it.

13.meaning: A noun meaning 'soul, self, person, living being.' It denotes the inner self or the whole individual — the seat of life and identity, and by extension a 'person' as a single unit.
13.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (with nunation): the genitive indefinite ('a soul'). This form appears after prepositions or in an 'of' linkage with a preceding noun (such as 'every soul').
13.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — soul, self, breath; the inner being

14.meaning: "and he will surely come to know" — the conjunction "and" with a marker of certain futurity attached to a verb meaning "to know," conveying that knowledge will definitely come to a single male subject in time.
14.grammar: Built from wa- ("and") plus the future prefix sa- ("will," indicating an action yet to come). The ya- prefix marks the subject as "he," and the -u ending is the indicative present marker. Together the prefixes turn "he knows" into "he will know."

15.meaning: the deniers, the ungrateful concealers — those who reject faith and cover over the truth; an intensive plural form stressing obstinate or repeated disbelief and ingratitude.
15.grammar: A definite plural noun: al- means "the," and kuffār is an intensive plural built on the doubled-middle pattern that stresses persistence in disbelief. The final -u is the nominative ending, generally marking the word as the subject of a sentence.
15.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to disbelieve, deny, conceal; to be ungrateful

16.meaning: 'for whoever / to the one who' — the preposition 'for/to' joined with the relative word 'who', introducing the person(s) about whom something is said.
16.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') combined with the relative/interrogative word 'man' ('who, whoever'). Together they single out a person or group as the focus ('for the one(s) who...').

17.meaning: The outcome, final result, or end-consequence of a matter; what ultimately comes after and follows from something — its sequel or final reward.
17.grammar: A feminine singular noun on the 'fuʿlā' pattern, denoting the end-result or aftermath of a course of action. Its final long 'ā' is fixed and does not change for the usual case-endings; as the first term of a possessive construction it conveys 'the outcome of …'.
17.root: ع-ق-ب (ʿ-q-b) — following after, succession, consequence, end-result

18.meaning: A noun meaning 'the abode' or 'the home' — a dwelling place. It frequently denotes a final, lasting abode (such as the eternal home of the Hereafter), as opposed to a temporary lodging.
18.grammar: A definite noun ('the abode') marked by the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The final '-i' ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('the … OF the abode') or follows a preposition. The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the 'd', doubling it (al-dār → ad-dār).
18.root: د-و-ر (d-w-r) — to turn, to encircle; a dwelling, abode

1.meaning: And he says, and he will say. A verb of speaking covering plain statement, and by extension holding an opinion or asking.
1.grammar: A present-tense verb for a single male ('he says/will say'), joined by wa- ('and'). The ya- prefix marks the third-person masculine singular subject. The final -u is the indicative ending, signalling a plain statement of fact (ongoing or future) rather than a command or a 'so that' clause.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
3.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

4.meaning: A negating verb meaning 'you are not' — it denies a present state or attribute of the person addressed.
4.grammar: A special verb of negation (from laysa) that denies being. The '-ta' ending marks a single male addressee: 'you (one man) are not.' It negates whatever description follows.

5.meaning: one who is sent — a person dispatched on a mission or commission; in religious usage, an envoy or messenger sent with a charge.
5.grammar: A passive participle ("one who is sent") formed with the mu- prefix. The ending -an is the indefinite accusative, which generally marks the word as the object of a verb or as a complement ("as a sent one"); the final -n (tanwīn) signals indefiniteness, like English "a/an."

6.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
6.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.
6.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak

7.meaning: "he/it sufficed" or "enough is …" — to be adequate and to spare, leaving no need for anything more. Used to declare that something or someone fully meets the need.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb from a root ending in a weak letter, so its final syllable appears as a long -ā. It reports a single completed action and, by its bare masculine form, takes "he/it" as subject. It commonly carries the sense "X is enough / X suffices."

8.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
8.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
8.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

9.meaning: 'A witness' — one who sees and attests, who can give evidence; also carries the sense of one who is present and observant, and at times 'a martyr' (one who bears witness with their life).
9.grammar: An intensive describing-noun (pattern fa‘īl) meaning 'a witness, one who fully attests', indefinite. The -an ending (the accusative with 'tanwīn') marks it as indefinite and in the accusative — the case used for a direct object, or for a word that describes the state or role in which someone stands.

10.meaning: 'Between me' — the spatial or relational word 'between' joined to 'me'. It marks the point or interval that lies on the speaker's side of a relationship between two parties.
10.grammar: The adverb/noun 'between' with the attached pronoun 'me'. 'Between' takes a following word in the genitive (linked-to) relation, and the -ī ending is the attached pronoun meaning 'me/my'.
10.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

11.meaning: 'And between you' — the word for 'between/among' joined by 'and', with 'you (all)' attached: the space, relation, or matter standing between you.
11.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') plus the adverb of place 'between' (fixed in the -a form), with the attached pronoun -kum ('you', masculine plural). Together they mean 'and between you (all)', marking a relation involving the addressees.
11.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

12.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
12.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

13.meaning: 'With him / in his keeping / that he has' — combining the locational word 'ind ('at, with, in the presence/possession of') with the pronoun 'him'. It conveys that something is held by, present with, or belongs to him.
13.grammar: 'ʿinda' is an adverb of place/possession that always governs a following word in the genitive; here it takes the attached pronoun -hu ('him/his'). The -a on 'ʿinda' is its fixed accusative-style ending as an adverbial. The pronoun -hu means the thing is located with, or owned by, a single male.

14.meaning: knowledge, knowing — sure awareness and understanding of something, the opposite of ignorance.
14.grammar: A noun meaning "knowledge." The final -u is the nominative ending, which generally marks the word as the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified; it also sets up a possessive link to a following noun ("the knowledge OF …").

15.meaning: the Book, the Scripture — a written record or revealed text; literally "that which is written," used especially for divinely revealed Scripture.
15.grammar: A definite noun: al- means "the." The -i ending is genitive, which typically links the word to a preceding noun in a possessive chain ("the … OF the Book") or follows a preposition.
